title: HalluciGuard-eye: knowledge graph-enhanced retrieval-augmented generation for hallucination detection and mitigation in ophthalmic multimodal large language models.
abstract: Background Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is the leading cause of preventable blindness in working-age adults, yet scalable early detection is limited by the unreliability of AI-assisted screening. Multimodal large language models can interpret fundus photographs and support DR grading, but they frequently hallucinate - fabricating lesions or misclassifying referable DR - which directly threatens timely treatment and prevention of vision loss. We developed HalluciGuard-Eye to make AI-assisted DR assessment trustworthy. Methods HalluciGuard-Eye combines knowledge graph-enhanced retrieval-augmented generation with hierarchical hallucination detection. An Ophthalmic Clinical Knowledge Graph containing 47,832 medical entities and 156,294 semantic relationships was constructed from clinical guidelines and published literature. A dual-stream architecture uses a Visual-Semantic Alignment Module to verify cross-modal consistency and a Clinical Factuality Grounding Network to anchor generated content to reranked evidence. The Hierarchical Factuality Score assesses anatomical, pathological, and clinical-recommendation accuracy. The framework was evaluated on four public ophthalmic imaging benchmarks. Results HalluciGuard-Eye reduced hallucination rates by 42.2% compared with state-of-the-art medical multimodal large language models and achieved 91.6% factual accuracy for clinical entity recognition on EyePACS. For diabetic retinopathy grading, sensitivity was 89.6% and specificity was 92.1%, representing improvements of 2.4% and 2.7%, respectively, over MedRAG. In the component ablation, removing knowledge-graph retrieval lowered EyePACS HFS by 9.4 percentage points. Additional analyses yielded 87.6% critical-evidence recall@20, 89.2% lesion-location accuracy, and 88.9% sensitivity in a patient-clustered cohort. Conclusions These results indicate that knowledge-grounded retrieval and hierarchical factuality assessment can reduce hallucinations while preserving diagnostic performance in ophthalmic multimodal language models.

title: Clinical and genetic features, surgical management, and longitudinal follow-up in two children with progressive osseous heteroplasia.
abstract: Background Progressive osseous heteroplasia (POH) is an ultrarare disorder characterized by heterotopic ossification that progresses from the skin and subcutaneous tissues into deeper connective tissues. Most affected individuals harbor heterozygous inactivating variants in GNAS , whereas postzygotic mosaic variants have rarely been described. Evidence to guide surgical management remains limited. Methods We retrospectively characterized two children with clinically diagnosed POH who underwent genetic testing and surgical treatment. Whole-exome sequencing was performed on peripheral blood and, when available, resected tissue, followed by PCR-Sanger sequencing and T-vector cloning. Case 1 underwent clinical and radiographic follow-up for 5 years; follow-up for Case 2 was limited to family-provided radiographs obtained at 2 years. Results Case 1 harbored a possible postzygotic mosaic GNAS variant, NM_000516.7:c.-1_2del, with variant allele frequencies of 14.7% in peripheral blood and 40.56% in bone lesion tissue. The predominantly localized wrist lesion was macroscopically excised. A small radiographic recurrence appeared by the second postoperative year but progressed slowly thereafter; active wrist flexion was 5-10 ° at 5 years. Case 2 harbored NM_000516.7:c.565_568del (p. (Asp189MetfsTer14)), detected as a heterozygous variant in peripheral blood. The lesion diffusely involved neurovascular structures, tendon sheaths, the joint capsule, and adjacent bones, precluding complete excision. Family-provided radiographs at 2 years showed an extent of ossification broadly similar to that before surgery; no in-person clinical assessment was available. Conclusion These cases provide additional clinical, molecular, and longitudinal information on POH and illustrate the importance of lesion distribution and resectability when interpreting surgical outcomes. The available postoperative findings cannot establish a causal relationship between variant status and prognosis because the patients differed in baseline disease extent, completeness of excision, follow-up duration, and outcome ascertainment. A possible association between mosaic burden and lesion distribution remains a hypothesis that requires evaluation in larger cohorts.

title: Chemotherapy-refractory high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma: single-cell findings, TCGA-OV transcriptomic context, and a single-case MRI-transcriptome illustration.
abstract: Background Primary chemotherapy refractoriness remains a clinical challenge in high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSC) and may reflect pre-existing tumor-cell states and microenvironmental heterogeneity. We examined public single-cell and bulk transcriptomic resources, a barcode-matched MRI case, and an in vitro cisplatin-perturbation RT-qPCR experiment. Methods We reanalyzed GSE300897, comprising 19,156 annotated cells from nine treatment-naïve HGSC biopsy libraries (four chemotherapy-refractory and five chemotherapy-sensitive), with response summaries retained at the library/patient level. The Cancer Genome Atlas Ovarian Cancer (TCGA-OV) provided 421 unique primary tumors for cohort-scale transcriptomic and overall survival context. One TCGA-OV case (TCGA-24-1423) linked a multiparametric MRI examination to a tumor RNA-seq barcode. OVCAR-3 and Caov-3 cells were exposed to cisplatin (5 μM, 24 h), and IFIT1, MX1, SNAI1, and HIF1A expression was measured by RT-qPCR. Results Across the nine GSE300897 libraries, no cancer-cell program passed Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) q < 0.05. Refractory libraries showed a lower type-I interferon (IFN-I) score (-0.15 log1p(CP10k)) and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) balance (-0.16), with a small increase in hypoxia (+0.05). In TCGA-OV, none of the six displayed program scores reached BH q < 0.05 in age- and stage-adjusted Cox models; IFN-I tertiles separated nominally by Kaplan-Meier analysis (log-rank p = 0.029), whereas continuous IFN-I was not significant after adjustment (HR = 0.96 per SD, BH q = 0.927). In TCGA-24-1423, the paired transcriptome showed an IFN-I score at the 86.8th TCGA-OV percentile, with IFIT1 and MX1 at the 87.5th and 93.7th percentiles. RT-qPCR showed lower IFIT1/MX1 and higher SNAI1/HIF1A after acute cisplatin exposure in both cell lines (all Holm-adjusted p < 0.05). Conclusion These findings support a conservative, hypothesis-generating interpretation of chemotherapy response-associated transcriptional heterogeneity in HGSC. Reduced IFN-I and altered cell-state programs were directional features of the small refractory single-cell cohort, whereas TCGA-OV provided context rather than independent response validation. The MRI-linked case demonstrates imaging-transcriptome pairing but does not establish an imaging biomarker. The RT-qPCR experiment demonstrates cisplatin-responsive changes in selected genes but models acute drug perturbation rather than the pretreatment clinical refractory state.

title: Pathology-guided multimodal transformer predicts postoperative survival benefit from adjuvant chemotherapy in glioma: from DNA damage repair to immune characterization.
abstract: Introduction High-grade gliomas (HGGs) are aggressive primary brain tumors with high recurrence rates and poor prognosis. Survival benefit from adjuvant temozolomide (TMZ) varies substantially across patients, and reliable preoperative biomarkers for treatment stratification remain limited. This study aims to develop an interpretable multimodal deep learning model integrating whole-slide histopathological images and multiparametric MRI to preoperatively predict survival benefit from adjuvant TMZ in HGG patients. Methods A Transformer-based multimodal fusion model was proposed. Key tumor regions were identified from whole-slide pathology images via weakly supervised clustering, and pathological features were extracted using attention-based multiple instance learning. Concurrently, 2.5D tumor subregional features were derived from multiparametric MRI sequences. These multimodal features were deeply fused using a Transformer encoder. The model was developed and validated on a multicenter cohort (504 patients), and its biological basis was explored through transcriptomic analysis, gene set enrichment analysis, protein-protein interaction networks, and immune deconvolution. Results The fusion model achieved AUCs of 0.910, 0.861, and 0.833 in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively. Transcriptomic analysis implicated DNA damage repair processes in high-benefit patients, suggesting that enhanced DNA repair capacity may contribute to TMZ sensitivity. Immune deconvolution showed higher M1 macrophage infiltration and lower regulatory T cell abundance in the high-benefit group, consistent with a less immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Importantly, low-benefit patients who completed TMZ chemotherapy had shorter survival than those treated with concurrent chemoradiotherapy alone or surgery alone. Conclusion This model identifies patients unlikely to benefit from standard TMZ chemotherapy, providing a tool for postoperative personalized treatment stratification and optimization of therapeutic strategies in HGGs.

title: Clinical variables and quantitative CT radiomics for mortality risk stratification after acute exacerbation of idiopathic inflammatory myopathy-associated interstitial lung disease.
abstract: Background Acute exacerbation (AE) is the most lethal event of idiopathic inflammatory myopathy-associated interstitial lung disease (IIM-ILD). This exploratory study compared clinical, radiomics, and combined predictor strategies across five survival-learning algorithms for survival risk stratification. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 78 patients with AE-IIM-ILD and divided them into a training cohort (n = 54; 20 deaths) and a held-out internal testing cohort (n = 24; 9 deaths), stratified by observed mortality event status. Three predictor strategies were evaluated: a clinical strategy comprising PaO 2 /FiO 2 ratio, neutrophil percentage (NEU%), and arthritis-related symptoms; a radiomics strategy comprising two selected radiomics features; and a combined strategy comprising PaO 2 /FiO 2 ratio, arthritis-related symptoms, and a composite radiomics score (Rad-score). Each strategy was evaluated using five survival-learning algorithms. Harrell's concordance index (C-index) was the primary discrimination metric, with mean time-dependent area under the curve (AUC) used as a secondary measure. Results During the 1-year follow-up, 29 deaths were observed. Performance rankings varied across predictor strategies, algorithms, and evaluation metrics. The combined-Random Survival Forest configuration demonstrated the highest training-cohort C-index among the 15 configurations. Its mean time-dependent AUC was 0.923 (95% CI: 0.860-0.970) in the training cohort and 0.915 (95% CI: 0.736-0.986) in the testing cohort, with corresponding C-indices of 0.874 (95% CI: 0.803-0.940) and 0.842 (95% CI: 0.673-0.971), respectively. The model stratified patients into high- and low-risk groups with distinct observed survival trajectories. Conclusion In this exploratory cohort, integrating selected clinical variables with a quantitative CT Rad-score using RSF showed promising numerical discrimination and risk-stratification performance. These findings suggest that clinical and quantitative imaging information may provide complementary prognostic information after AE-IIM-ILD.

title: Case Report: Cholangioscopic and histopathological findings before and after treatment in immune-related cholangitis.
abstract: Immune-related cholangitis is a rare immune-related adverse event, and its diagnostic criteria and treatment strategies have not yet been established. Here, we report a case of immune-related cholangitis in which treatment response could be objectively visualized through reassessment of cholangioscopic and histopathological findings before and after treatment. A 79-year-old man with recurrent cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma of the scalp developed high fever and general fatigue after six courses of nivolumab, and laboratory tests revealed marked elevation of hepatobiliary enzymes. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography and endoscopic ultrasonography showed bile duct wall thickening, endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography demonstrated shaggy irregularity in the distal bile duct, and peroral cholangioscopy revealed diffuse surface irregularity and granular changes of the biliary mucosa. Furthermore, cholangioscopy-guided bile duct biopsy demonstrated marked lymphocytic infiltration, particularly infiltration of CD8-positive T cells, leading to a diagnosis of immune-related cholangitis. Prednisolone and ursodeoxycholic acid were initiated, with nivolumab discontinued, after which the clinical symptoms and hepatobiliary enzyme levels gradually improved. Furthermore, on Day 28 after treatment initiation, reassessment by cholangioscopy and bile duct biopsy confirmed improvement in the cholangioscopic findings and reduction of lymphocytic infiltration, particularly CD8-positive T-cell infiltration, on bile duct biopsy. These objective findings supported tapering of steroid therapy. To our knowledge, very few cases have described reassessment of cholangioscopic and histopathological findings before and after treatment in immune-related cholangitis. We suggest that such evaluation may contribute to confirming treatment response and guiding therapeutic strategy in immune-related cholangitis.

title: Neurexin-3α IgG-mediated autoimmune encephalitis with psychiatric manifestations and choreiform movements: a case report and literature review.
abstract: To summarize the clinical manifestations, ancillary examination findings, treatment course, and prognosis of a patient with neurexin-3α IgG-mediated autoimmune encephalitis presenting with prominent psychiatric disturbances and choreiform movements, and to review the literature on the clinical spectrum of this disease. A 52-year-old woman with a history of hypertension and biopsy-proven podocytopathy with a "full-house" immunofluorescence pattern showing diffuse positivity for IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, and C1q, diagnosed in February 2026; however, a definitive diagnosis of lupus podocytopathy remained uncertain, as the patient lacked systemic lupus erythematosus manifestations. She was admitted on April 3, 2026, with a 5-day history of psychiatric disturbances and involuntary choreiform movements in all four limbs, preceded by significant psychological stress (bereavement). Neurological examination revealed slowed responses and impaired calculation. Cranial MRI showed only bilateral periventricular small ischemic foci (Fazekas grade 1) with normal SWI. Initial EEG demonstrated sharp waves and spike-and-wave complexes in the left parietal, occipital, and temporal regions. CSF analysis revealed leukocytosis (21/μl, 90% mononuclear cells), protein of 0.4 g/L, elevated IgG index of 0.76, and elevated 24-hour intrathecal IgG synthesis rate of 5.63 mg/dl. CSF mNGS detected 453 EBV sequences (RPM) with a relative abundance of 97.48%. Serum EBV VCA-IgG and EBNA-IgG were elevated with negative IgM. Autoantibody testing followed a stepwise approach: initial screening for conventional autoimmune encephalitis, paraneoplastic, and demyelinating antibodies was negative; subsequent tissue-based assay (TBA) of CSF revealed strong positive immunoreactivity, prompting expanded antibody panel testing, which ultimately detected anti-neurexin-3α antibodies in serum (titer 1:30) and CSF (titer 1:100), confirmed by both cell-based assay (CBA) and TBA. The patient's condition progressively deteriorated, requiring endotracheal intubation on April 21 and tracheostomy on April 30. She received methylprednisolone pulse therapy at 500 mg/day for 5 days followed by a stepwise taper, intravenous immunoglobulin at 0.4 g/kg for 5 days, and five sessions of plasma exchange from April 30 to May 8 due to poor initial response. Choreiform movements gradually resolved after plasma exchange. She was weaned from mechanical ventilation on May 19 and decannulated on May 27. During the ICU course, she developed pulmonary infection with carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii, which was controlled after antibiotic adjustment. Repeat EEG normalized on June 1. She was discharged from rehabilitation on June 9 on oral methylprednisolone 32 mg/day. On June 26, 2026, follow-up serum TBA showed weakly positive immunoreactivity, with the serum antibody titer remaining at 1:30. She subsequently received four infusions of efgartigimod at 400 mg each for consolidation immunotherapy and was transitioned to ofatumumab for long-term maintenance. At follow-up on August 6, 2026, the patient had no residual psychiatric symptoms or choreiform movements, with muscle strength recovered to 4+ in all limbs, full independence in daily activities, ambulation without assistance, and only mild gait instability. Neurexin-3α IgG-mediated autoimmune encephalitis is a rare but treatable condition. Choreiform movements expand its clinical spectrum. The coexistence of podocytopathy raises a hypothesis of shared antigenicity between renal and neuronal neurexin family members, though this remains purely speculative. CSF EBV reactivation may represent a bystander phenomenon or epiphenomenon of severe immune dysregulation rather than a confirmed trigger. Tissue-based assay provides crucial diagnostic direction when conventional screening is negative. Early recognition, comprehensive immunotherapy, and meticulous ICU management are important determinants of favorable outcomes. Given the inherent limitations of a single case report, these findings warrant confirmation through larger cohort studies.

title: Gut microbiota and innate immune barrier dysfunction in hepatic portal venous gas: a hypothesis-generating review.
abstract: Hepatic portal venous gas (HPVG) is an uncommon radiographic sign whose prognosis is driven by bowel necrosis and shock rather than by intraportal gas. Immunological events along the gut-liver axis have not been synthesized for adult HPVG, and dedicated microbiome, metabolomic, gut-vascular barrier (GVB), and immune-profiling data are lacking. This hypothesis-generating review proposes gut dysbiosis as a putative contributor to mucosal and hepatic innate immune failure, inferred from cirrhosis, porto-sinusoidal vascular disease (PSVD), and intestinal ischemia/reperfusion. In those proxy states, loss of acetyl-CoA butyrate-production capacity, context-dependent bile-acid shifts, lipopolysaccharide-Toll-like receptor 4 priming, facultative-anaerobe expansion, and fermentative H 2 /CO 2 pathways documented in cultured HPVG isolates-Clostridium perfringens (pyruvate-ferredoxin oxidoreductase-hydrogenase) and Escherichia coli (pyruvate-formate lyase-formate hydrogen lyase)-compromise epithelial and GVB integrity. These links are not assembled as a demonstrated sequence in adult HPVG. We propose a physical-core model in which a route of entry and a local driving pressure gradient are necessary, whereas pathway-defined fermentative isolates, dysbiosis, mucosal inflammation, ischemia, and impaired portal clearance are optional amplifiers. Iatrogenic or purely pressure-related HPVG can occur without dysbiosis or a substantial pathogen-associated molecular pattern load; in necrosis-driven HPVG, dysbiosis is proposed only as a concurrent immune amplifier; when HPVG occurs in cirrhosis or PSVD, portal hypertension is treated as a host modifier of barrier geometry and washout, not as an independent generator of intraportal gas. Portal vein thrombosis, portal hypertension, pneumatosis intestinalis, pyogenic liver abscess, and HPVG may share the portal vein as a conduit but are not interchangeable. No microbiota-directed intervention has been tested against an HPVG endpoint and none should delay source control; probiotics, rifaximin, fecal microbiota transplantation, diet, and phage remain research questions.

title: Beyond tessellation: AI-derived choroidal vessel density on multi-channel cSLO as a surrogate biomarker for OCT choroidal parameters.
abstract: Purpose To develop an AI-based method for quantifying choroidal vessel density (CVD) from ultra-widefield confocal scanning laser ophthalmoscopy (UWF-cSLO) and to validate this metric against swept-source optical coherence tomography (SS-OCT) choroidal parameters. Methods In this retrospective cross-sectional study, 633 eyes from 354 participants underwent simultaneous UWF-cSLO and SS-OCT imaging on an integrated platform, ensuring precise spatial co-registration. A TransUNet deep-learning model segmented choroidal vessels from red-channel (R; 665 nm) and infrared-channel (IR; 785 nm) images, yielding channel-specific metrics (R-CVD and IR-CVD) and a combined metric (IR + R CVD). Eight SS-OCT parameters-including choroidal thickness (CT), choroidal vascularity index (CVI), luminal area, stromal area (SA), total choroidal area (TCA), and vessel volume index (VVI)-served as reference measures. Associations were evaluated using Spearman correlations with participant-level clustered bootstrap confidence intervals, multivariable generalised estimating equations (GEE) adjusted for age and sex, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Results Segmentation accuracy exceeded 0.95 (Dice coefficient) in both channels. R-CVD exhibited the strongest inverse correlations with structural and volumetric OCT parameters (SA: ρ = -0.619; CT: ρ = -0.615; TCA: ρ = -0.615; all q < 0.001), whereas IR + R CVD correlated most closely with proportion-based indices (VVI: ρ = -0.34; CVI: ρ = -0.29). These channel-dependent patterns persisted after adjustment for age and sex in multivariable GEE models. On ROC analysis, R-CVD discriminated thin from thick choroids with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.789 (sensitivity 72.5%; specificity 74.8%), whereas IR-CVD alone showed near-chance performance (AUC 0.517). Conclusions AI-derived CVD from UWF-cSLO correlates strongly with SS-OCT choroidal parameters in a wavelength-dependent manner and may serve as an accessible surrogate for choroidal structural assessment in settings without OCT.

title: Case Report: Longitudinal multimodal imaging and microperimetry findings in PAMM: apparent capillary rarefaction and persistent sensitivity loss across 28 months.
abstract: Introduction Paracentral acute middle maculopathy (PAMM) is classically associated with retinal vascular occlusion or systemic vasculopathy. We describe an atypical presentation of isolated PAMM occurring in close temporal association with the abrupt withdrawal of systemic pharmacotherapy in the setting of isolated marked proteinuria, including a 28-month longitudinal analysis of structural and functional outcomes. Patient presentation A 37-year-old male with a history of asymptomatic proteinuria presented with acute paracentral scotomas shortly after discontinuing a short course of azilsartan and hydroxychloroquine. Multimodal imaging, including spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) and OCT angiography (OCTA), revealed focal inner nuclear layer (INL) infarction and deep capillary plexus (DCP) hypoperfusion, consistent with isolated PAMM in the absence of macroscopic vascular occlusion. The patient received hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) during the acute phase; a subsequent transient improvement in localized retinal sensitivity was observed, but best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) stabilized at 20/40. However, serial microperimetry demonstrated a transient improvement in localized macular sensitivity from 3 weeks to 9 weeks post-onset, followed by a marked secondary decline from 9 weeks to 28 months. This late-stage functional loss was topographically coupled with progressive INL and outer plexiform layer (OPL) atrophy, alongside apparent capillary rarefaction on OCTA. Conclusions Acute hemodynamic changes following medication withdrawal, combined with a potential hypercoagulability or prothrombotic risk from proteinuria, may have contributed to the development of isolated PAMM. The long-term visual prognosis is closely associated with progressive microvascular dropout and retinal atrophy. Serial microperimetry is essential to evaluate the true functional impairment in these patients.

title: From MRI-defined bone marrow lesions to pain, structural progression, and subchondral remodeling in knee osteoarthritis: an integrated multi-database bibliometric and text-mining analysis.
abstract: Objective To characterize the publication landscape, intellectual structure, thematic evolution, and emerging clinical, mechanistic, and translational directions of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-defined bone marrow lesion (BML) research in knee osteoarthritis. Methods Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, and PubMed were searched using core concepts related to knee osteoarthritis, MRI, and BMLs or bone marrow edema-like lesions. The searches initially identified 2,452 records, of which 2,415 were exported after database-level filters. Following cross-database deduplication, eligibility assessment, and application of the prespecified publication cutoff, 726 publications constituted the final integrated corpus. Descriptive bibliometrics, collaboration-network analysis, reference co-citation analysis, keyword and MeSH mapping, temporal thematic analysis, term frequency-inverse document frequency-based document clustering, and dictionary-based bridge-theme mapping were performed. Candidate cluster solutions from k = 2 to k = 10 were evaluated using within-cluster sum of squares, silhouette width, gap statistics, and repeated-subsample stability. Results Publication activity increased substantially from 1996 through 2025, with the partial 2026 count reflecting publications available by June 1. Osteoarthritis and Cartilage was the leading journal, and the United States, Australia, Germany, China, and the United Kingdom were the major contributing countries. The knowledge base was anchored by studies of whole-joint MRI assessment, BML-related pain, structural progression, and imaging-pathology interpretation. Six exploratory text-derived research domains were identified: post-traumatic and surgical BML outcomes; community-based structural and risk correlates; subchondral biology, biomarkers, and mechanisms; longitudinal whole-joint progression and symptoms; pharmacologic, biologic, and interventional treatment; and MRI quantification and methodological validation. No single diagnostic identified a uniquely optimal cluster number; the six-domain solution was retained as an interpretable intermediate-granularity representation with moderate resampling stability. Exclusion of the 28 publications dated 2026 did not materially alter the publication trajectory, leading recent terms, or temporal-theme prevalence. Conclusion MRI-defined BML research in knee osteoarthritis has developed into a multidisciplinary field connecting imaging phenotypes with symptoms, structural progression, subchondral remodeling, biomechanics, inflammation, and treatment-oriented investigation. Future studies should integrate longitudinal lesion trajectories, quantitative imaging, adjacent joint pathology, biomechanical measures, biological markers, and pain phenotyping to clarify clinically meaningful BML subtypes and their therapeutic implications.

title: Intratumoral susceptibility signals in adult-type diffuse gliomas: associations with molecular profile, tumor grade, and overall survival.
abstract: Purpose Intratumoral Susceptibility Signals (ITSS) are low-signal-intensity structures observed on susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) which may reflect intratumoral microhemorrhages, calcifications, and neovascularization. Previous studies have demonstrated associations between ITSS, glioma grade, and molecular characteristics; however, their potential role in outcome prediction remains incompletely defined. This study investigated the diagnostic and and potential prognostic role of ITSS in adult diffuse gliomas. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 128 adult patients with histologically confirmed diffuse gliomas who underwent preoperative MRI including SWI. ITSS were graded from 0 to 3 according to the number of susceptibility signals. Associations between ITSS grade and CNS WHO tumor grade, IDH mutation status, MGMT promoter methylation and Ki-67 labeling index (LI) were evaluated. Overall survival (OS) was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models. Results ITSS grade was significantly associated with WHO glioma grade ( p < 0.001), with lower-grade tumors predominantly exhibiting ITSS grades 0-1 and higher-grade gliomas showing grades 2-3. IDH-mutant gliomas displayed significantly lower ITSS grades than IDH-wildtype tumors ( p < 0.001). ITSS grade was positively correlated with Ki-67 labeling index (Spearman's ρ = 0.423, p < 0.001). In the survival cohort ( n = 87) higher ITSS burden was significantly associated with shorter OS (ITSS 2-3 vs. 0-1: HR = 3.19, 95% CI 1.65-6.19; p < 0.001). However, this association was no longer significant after adjustment for established prognostic factors (HR = 1.40, 95% CI 0.69-2.86; p = 0.350), with IDH status emerging as the strongest independent association with shorter OS. Conclusion ITSS grading on SWI is associated with CNS WHO grade, molecular profile, proliferative activity, and OS in adult-type diffuse gliomas. Although ITSS was not an independent predictor of survival after adjustment for established prognostic factors, it may serve as a readily available, non-invasive imaging correlate of tumor aggressiveness, providing complementary information for preoperative tumor characterization while definitive molecular data are pending.

title: Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, with spontaneous transdural and calvarial invasion: a case report and literature review.
abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM), IDH-wildtype, is the most aggressive adult-type diffuse glioma. Although extracranial spread may occur after craniotomy, radiotherapy, or other interventions, spontaneous transdural and calvarial invasion before treatment is exceedingly rare. We report a 37-year-old woman who presented with long-standing right temporal-parietal headache and acute worsening with vomiting. Computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a right temporal mass with intratumoral hemorrhage, peritumoral edema, and contiguous extension through the dura and temporal bone into the temporalis muscle. The lesion was resected through a transcranial approach, and postoperative imaging showed gross total resection. Histological examination demonstrated an infiltrating high-grade glial neoplasm with brisk mitotic activity and palisading necrosis. Immunohistochemical and molecular findings, including the absence of IDH1/IDH2 mutations, supported a diagnosis of glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, CNS WHO grade 4. At 18 months after surgery, the patient remained alive. This case highlights a rare pattern of primary extracranial extension in GBM and suggests direct contiguous transdural invasion as a plausible route of spread in the absence of prior intervention.

title: Assessing early therapeutic response in extrapulmonary tuberculosis using [18F]FDG-PET/CT imaging.
abstract: Introduction Monitoring treatment response in extrapulmonary tuberculosis (EPTB) remains challenging due to limited microbiological accessibility and the lack of validated biomarkers. [18F]FDG positron emission tomography/computed tomography [(18F)FDG-PET/CT] enables assessment of metabolic disease activity and has been explored in infectious diseases, but evidence supporting its use in EPTB is limited. Methods We conducted a prospective observational study including adults diagnosed with EPTB at a tertiary referral center in Denmark between 2016 and 2018. Participants underwent baseline and follow-up [18F]FDG-PET/CT imaging after completion of the intensive treatment phase. Clinical data and laboratory parameters, including C-reactive protein (CRP), hemoglobin, leukocytes, albumin, and alanine aminotransferase were collected at baseline and during follow-up. Changes in standardized uptake values (SUVmax) and laboratory markers were analyzed descriptively. Results Seventeen patients were included. Metabolically active disease was detected in all participants at baseline. Most patients (11 out of 14) demonstrated a reduction in lesion number and SUVmax at follow-up, indicating a metabolic response to therapy. However, persistent [18F]FDG uptake was observed in a subset of patients (3 out of 14). Median CRP levels declined from 12 mg/L (range: 0.3-190) at baseline to 3.6 mg/L (range: 0.9-20) at week 8 and remained low thereafter, broadly paralleling PET/CT findings. In several cases, residual metabolic activity did not result in treatment prolongation. Discussion Serial [18F]FDG-PET/CT demonstrated changes in metabolic activity during treatment with reductions in lesion number and SUVmax in most patients. However, SUVmax reflects focal metabolic activity rather than total disease burden, and persistent uptake after the intensive treatment phase was observed in some patients. Larger prospective studies incorporating standardized response criteria and volumetric PET measures are needed before [18F]FDG-PET/CT can be implemented as a routine biomarker for treatment response in EPTB.

Larger prospective studies incorporating standardized response criteria and volumetric PET measures are needed before [18F]FDG-PET/CT can be implemented as a routine biomarker for treatment response in EPTB.

title: Multi-sequence magnetic resonance imaging radiomics integrated with clinical features predicts pelvic lymph node metastasis in cervical cancer: a retrospective-prospective cohort study.
abstract: Background Pelvic lymph node metastasis is a major determinant of staging, recurrence risk, and treatment selection in cervical cancer, yet conventional magnetic resonance imaging criteria based on nodal size and morphology remain insufficient for occult nodal disease. We developed and temporally validated a multi-sequence magnetic resonance imaging radiomics-clinical fusion framework for pretreatment prediction of pelvic lymph node metastasis. Methods This single-center retrospective-prospective cohort study included 200 women with histologically confirmed cervical cancer who underwent pretreatment pelvic magnetic resonance imaging. A retrospective training cohort ( n = 100) was accrued from January 2018 to December 2022, and a prospective temporal validation cohort ( n = 100) was accrued from January 2023 to December 2024. Reference standards comprised surgical histopathology in 154 patients and composite clinical-imaging adjudication in 46 patients. Primary tumors were manually segmented on axial T2-weighted imaging and registered to T1-weighted imaging, diffusion-weighted imaging/apparent diffusion coefficient maps, and dynamic contrast-enhanced imaging. An Image Biomarker Standardisation Initiative-compliant radiomics pipeline was used, including resampling, intensity discretization, reproducibility filtering, correlation pruning, and nested feature selection. Clinical, radiomics, clinical-radiomics, and deep fusion models were evaluated in the prospective cohort using discrimination, calibration, decision-curve, and reclassification analyses. Results The deep fusion model achieved the best validation discrimination, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.910 (95% confidence interval, 0.845-0.959) and an area under the precision-recall curve of 0.849. At the training-derived threshold, accuracy was 0.84, sensitivity was 0.79, specificity was 0.86, positive predictive value was 0.75, negative predictive value was 0.89, and Brier score was 0.125. Deep fusion outperformed the clinical model (area under the curve, 0.730; mean delta area under the curve, 0.180; P < 0.001) and improved reclassification relative to the clinical model. Conclusion Multi-sequence magnetic resonance imaging radiomics-clinical fusion improved pretreatment risk stratification for pelvic lymph node metastasis in cervical cancer. External multicenter validation is warranted before clinical implementation. These preliminary single-center findings should be interpreted cautiously and require multicenter external validation before broad clinical implementation.

title: Artificial intelligence for ophthalmic vessel segmentation: from multimodal imaging to clinical translation.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-based vessel segmentation converts color fundus photographs, scanning laser ophthalmoscopy (SLO), optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA), structural OCT, and anterior-segment images into quantitative vascular biomarkers. Strong performance within individual datasets has not consistently yielded reliable clinical measurements because errors can arise during acquisition, anatomical preprocessing, vessel extraction, biomarker calculation, and deployment. This structured narrative review compares segmentation tasks involving retinal vascular trees, OCTA capillary plexuses, the structural choroid and choriocapillaris, macular neovascularization, corneal neovascularization, and conjunctival microvasculature. We assess modern architectures in relation to vessel geometry, severe foreground-background imbalance, scale variation, crossings, and susceptibility to artifacts. The methods considered include multiscale feature pyramids, deformable and directional operators, Transformers, state-space models, diffusion approaches, and foundation models. We organize the synthesis around five evaluation levels: pixel overlap, centerline recovery, vascular topology, biomarker agreement, and clinical actionability. Public fundus and OCTA datasets are catalogued with their acquisition and annotation characteristics, and gaps in public anterior-segment vessel benchmarks are discussed. Because devices, data splits, labels, and post-processing differ substantially, reported metrics are summarized without ranking studies against one another. The review distinguishes structural OCT choroidal vascularity index from OCTA choriocapillaris flow-deficit mapping, as well as true vessel segmentation from global hyperemia grading. Clinical translation will require ocular-magnification correction, quality control of retinal layers and projection artifacts, external testing across devices and populations, out-of-distribution rejection, DICOM/PACS interoperability, prospective impact studies, and regulation as software as a medical device. We conclude that clinical utility depends on an auditable pipeline that measures structural error, biomarker uncertainty, and failure states throughout the workflow.

title: Artificial intelligence in spinal fracture imaging: from clinical application to translational promise.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping medical imaging, and deep learning together with machine learning are now being used to detect, classify, and differentially diagnose spinal fractures. In this Review, we survey the principal AI architectures that currently support spinal imaging, including convolutional neural networks, object detectors, and hybrid models, and we assess their reported performance for osteoporotic, traumatic, and pathological vertebral fractures. Our synthesis indicates that AI can achieve high diagnostic accuracy in controlled, often single-centre retrospective settings, but its performance consistently declines for mild fractures, degenerated spines, and postoperative anatomy. Critically, the majority of published models lack external validation, and many studies suffer from methodological shortcomings such as selective reporting, insufficient sample sizes, and absence of predefined analysis plans-factors that systematically inflate apparent accuracy. Beyond detection, we explore the growing applications of AI in surgical planning, complication prediction, and functional outcome estimation, while emphasising that most evidence remains preliminary. We identify persistent gaps, including underuse of foundation models and public benchmarks, and limited independent evaluation of commercial tools. We conclude by proposing a shift from performance reporting to methodologically rigorous, prospectively designed studies that incorporate bias assessment, standardised reporting, and patient-centred endpoints-steps essential to translate technical promise into tangible patient benefit.

title: Association of Serum GDF-15 with Bone and Muscle Parameters in Community-Dwelling Individuals.
abstract: Introduction Muscle mass and bone mineral density decrease with aging, although following different patterns among males and females. Growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF-15) is a stress-induced cytokine and has emerged as a key biomarker for inflammation, tissue injury, and metabolic stress. We tested the association between GDF-15 and specific bone and muscle parameters in a large cohort of community-dwelling subjects. Methods The SardiNIA survey included 4,842 subjects (2,795 females). All underwent a detailed medical visit and laboratory testing. Peripheral quantitative computed tomography at the tibia was performed to evaluate volumetric bone mineral density and bone microstructure as well as muscle mass. Results Multivariate regression analysis showed that GDF-15 was negatively associated with cortical bone density (Beta -0.042, p < 0.001) in females. In males, total bone density and trabecular bone density at 4% site and cortical bone area at 38% site were negatively associated with GDF-15 levels (respectively, Beta -0.016, p = 0.027, Beta -0.014, p = 0.039, and Beta -0.022, p = 0.002). Multivariate regression analysis for muscle parameters showed that GDF-15 was negatively associated with muscle density (Beta -0.002 in females and males, p < 0.001 for all) and muscle area (Beta -0.338, p = 0.003, Beta -0.744, p < 0.001). Conclusions Higher circulating GDF-15 levels were independently associated with lower volumetricBMD and poorer muscle parameters in both women and men. These findings support the potential role of GDF-15 as a biomarker of age-related musculoskeletal decline, although longitudinal studies are needed to determine whether GDF-15 contributes to the development of these changes or simply reflects the underlying biological processes.

title: Clinical utility and reproducibility of intravoxel incoherent motion MRI in rectal cancer: a structured narrative review.
abstract: Introduction Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is a crucial imaging modality for the management of rectal cancer. Conventional MRI provides detailed anatomical information but has a limited capacity to evaluate tumor biology. Intravoxel Incoherent Motion (IVIM) is an advanced functional MRI technique that simultaneously measures tissue cellularity and microvascular perfusion without contrast agents, providing deeper insights into the tumor microenvironment. This narrative review critically examines the current evidence on the clinical usefulness of IVIM MRI in rectal cancer, focusing on three key areas: tumor characterization and staging, prediction and monitoring of treatment response, and the reproducibility and limitations of IVIM parameters. Methods A literature search was conducted in vid MEDLINE, PubMed, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, and Google Scholar from 2015 to October 2025. The search included keywords such as "intravoxel incoherent motion OR IVIM" and "rectal cancer OR colorectal cancer." Original studies with at least 10 patients were included; reviews, case reports, and animal studies were excluded. Results The true diffusion coefficient D appears to be the most biologically interpretable and reproducible IVIM-derived parameter, with several studies linking lower D values to greater cellularity or more aggressive tumor features; however, findings are not uniform across all cohorts. While the perfusion fraction (f) has shown associations with markers of aggressiveness in some studies, its clinical utility is limited by poor reproducibility. For nodal staging, primary-tumor IVIM histogram models have shown promising diagnostic performance, although most evidence remains from single centers and is insufficiently validated. When assessing the response to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT), a post-treatment increase in D appears to be the most consistent IVIM-derived marker of treatment response. However, its clinical use still requires standardized acquisition and external validation while perfusion parameters (f and D*) exhibit poor test-retest reproducibility. Combining IVIM with complementary techniques, such as diffusion kurtosis imaging or radiomics, may improve predictive performance compared with individual parameters. Conclusion IVIM-DWI provides non-contrast quantitative information on diffusion and perfusion in rectal cancer. Current evidence suggests that D is the most reproducible and biologically interpretable IVIM parameter, whereas f and D* remain limited by poor repeatability and protocol dependence. IVIM may add value for tumor characterization, nodal risk assessment, and treatment-response evaluation, particularly when combined with histogram analysis, DKI, or radiomics; however, standardized acquisition protocols and external validation are required before routine clinical implementation.

title: Intracranial metastasis following intrahepatic remission in primary hepatic small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma: a case report.
abstract: Background Hepatogenic small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (HP-SCNEC) is a highly aggressive rare malignancy, with central nervous system (CNS) metastasis being a major cause of treatment failure. This case report describes a patient with extensively metastatic HP-SCNEC, aiming to explore the clinical features of rapid brain metastasis following complete remission of intrahepatic lesions, as well as corresponding multidisciplinary treatment strategies. Method A retrospective analysis of the diagnostic and therapeutic process in a 60-year-old female patient with HP-SCNEC. At initial presentation, the patient exhibited multiple intrahepatic metastases, abdominal lymph node involvement, and adrenal metastases. First-line therapy comprised the programmed death receptor-1 (PD-1) inhibitor sintilimab combined with etoposide and cisplatin. Following disease progression, whole-brain radiotherapy was administered for newly identified brain metastases, concurrently with systemic treatment adjustment to albumin-bound paclitaxel combined with anlotinib. Results Following 6 cycles of immunotherapy combined with chemotherapy and 2 cycles of immunotherapy combined with anti-angiogenic therapy, the patient achieved radiographic complete remission of hepatic lesions. However, merely 16 days after achieving this remission, the patient presented with new-onset neurological symptoms, and subsequent imaging confirmed multiple new brain metastases. After undergoing whole-brain radiotherapy combined with an adjusted systemic treatment regimen, intracranial lesions were effectively controlled. The patient remained stable during subsequent maintenance therapy with Anlotinib. Conclusion This case demonstrates that even when HP-SCNEC abdominal lesions achieve deep remission through intensified immunotherapy combined with chemotherapy, patients remain at extremely high risk for early brain metastases, highlighting the "intracranial sanctuary" effect caused by the blood-brain barrier. For such patients, prevention and monitoring of central nervous system metastases must be prioritized during initial treatment. Following brain metastasis, a multimodal comprehensive strategy centered on radiotherapy combined with intracranial active drugs should be adopted. This case provides important reference for the comprehensive management of this rare malignant tumor.

title: Robot-assisted navigation combined with a double reverse traction reduction frame for retrograde intramedullary nailing of extra-articular distal femoral fractures: a retrospective comparative cohort study.
abstract: Objective To compare the perioperative, radiographic, and functional outcomes associated with an integrated surgical workflow combining robot-assisted navigation with a double reverse traction reduction frame vs. conventional manual traction. Methods This retrospective comparative cohort study was conducted on 58 patients (AO/OTA 33-A1 or 33-A2) with distal femoral fractures treated between January 2021 and December 2024. Patients were divided into a robot-assisted double reverse traction reduction group (RDR group, n = 26) and a conventional manual traction group (CMT group, n = 32). All patients underwent retrograde intramedullary nailing. The RDR group received robot-assisted guidewire positioning combined with continuous traction-frame-assisted fracture reduction, whereas the CMT group underwent conventional manual traction reduction. Perioperative parameters, radiographic outcomes, functional scores, and complications were analyzed. Results The groups were similar in the measured baseline demographic and fracture characteristics, including AO/OTA subtype. Compared with the CMT group, the RDR group showed significantly reduced operative time, decreased intraoperative blood loss, fewer fluoroscopic acquisitions, smaller residual coronal and sagittal angulation, and shorter fracture healing time. At the 12-month follow-up, knee flexion angle and Hospital for Special Surgery (HSS) knee score were significantly higher in the RDR group. No significant difference in complication rates was observed between groups. Conclusion In this retrospective comparative cohort, the integrated workflow was associated with shorter operative time, lower intraoperative blood loss, fewer fluoroscopic acquisitions, improved postoperative alignment, and better 12-month knee function compared with conventional manual traction.

title: Dual-phase CTA filling pattern is associated with reperfusion-related complications after mechanical thrombectomy in late-window anterior circulation stroke.
abstract: Objective To evaluate whether pre-treatment dual-phase computed tomography angiography (CTA) filling patterns are independently associated with reperfusion-related complications after late-window mechanical thrombectomy and whether they provide incremental prognostic value beyond conventional clinical and imaging variables. Methods We conducted a prospective single-center cohort study including 80 consecutive patients with anterior circulation large-vessel occlusion who underwent mechanical thrombectomy within 6-24 h after stroke onset or last known well. Dual-phase CTA filling patterns were classified as good early filling, delayed filling, or persistent poor filling; delayed and persistent poor filling were combined for the primary analyses. The primary outcome was a composite of reperfusion-related complications within 72 h, including hemorrhagic transformation ≥HI2, malignant cerebral edema, or early neurological deterioration. Secondary outcomes were 90-day functional independence and all-cause mortality. Independent predictors were identified using Firth penalized logistic regression. Incremental model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis, bootstrap internal validation, reclassification metrics, and decision-curve analysis. Results Reperfusion-related complications occurred in 28 patients (35%) and were significantly more frequent in patients with delayed or poor filling than in those with good early filling (56% vs. 20%; p < 0.001). Delayed or poor filling independently predicted reperfusion-related complications after adjustment for age, baseline NIHSS score, and ASPECTS (adjusted OR 3.97, 95% CI 1.22-14.10; p = 0.022). Older age was also independently associated with increased risk (adjusted OR 2.14 per 10-year increase, 95% CI 1.24-4.12; p = 0.005), whereas higher ASPECTS was protective (adjusted OR 0.35 per point, 95% CI 0.18-0.61; p < 0.001). The full model incorporating dual-phase CTA achieved excellent discrimination (AUC 0.895; optimism-corrected AUC 0.867). Addition of the dual-phase CTA filling pattern improved patient risk reclassification, although the increase in discrimination beyond the clinical-plus-ASPECTS model was not statistically significant. Patients with delayed or poor filling had substantially worse 90-day outcomes, including lower functional independence (24% vs. 70%) and higher mortality (38% vs. 4%) (both p < 0.001). Conclusions Delayed or persistent poor filling on dual-phase CTA is an independent imaging marker of reperfusion-related complications following late-window mechanical thrombectomy. Although its incremental contribution to model discrimination was modest, dual-phase CTA may improve early risk stratification and help identify patients who may benefit from intensified post-procedural monitoring. External validation is warranted before routine clinical implementation.

Older age was also independently associated with increased risk (adjusted OR 2.14 per 10-year increase, 95% CI 1.24-4.12; p = 0.005), whereas higher ASPECTS was protective (adjusted OR 0.35 per point, 95% CI 0.18-0.61; p < 0.001). The full model incorporating dual-phase CTA achieved excellent discrimination (AUC 0.895; optimism-corrected AUC 0.867). Addition of the dual-phase CTA filling pattern improved patient risk reclassification, although the increase in discrimination beyond the clinical-plus-ASPECTS model was not statistically significant. Patients with delayed or poor filling had substantially worse 90-day outcomes, including lower functional independence (24% vs. 70%) and higher mortality (38% vs. 4%) (both p < 0.001).

Conclusions

Delayed or persistent poor filling on dual-phase CTA is an independent imaging marker of reperfusion-related complications following late-window mechanical thrombectomy. Although its incremental contribution to model discrimination was modest, dual-phase CTA may improve early risk stratification and help identify patients who may benefit from intensified post-procedural monitoring. External validation is warranted before routine clinical implementation.

title: AI-driven CT assessment of erector spinae myosteatosis: muscle quality and its association with strength and frailty in older surgical patients.
abstract: Background Frailty and sarcopenia are overlapping syndromes that increase adverse outcomes in older adults. Computed tomography (CT) is a reference standard for body composition analysis, but manual segmentation is time-consuming. This exploratory study used a fully automated deep learning model (DLM) to investigate associations between CT-derived muscle quality and quantity and clinical frailty. Methods We performed a retrospective, cross-sectional secondary analysis of 53 geriatric surgical patients (mean age 77.4 ± 4.4 years). A DLM segmented skeletal muscle (SM), subcutaneous and visceral adipose tissue at the third lumbar vertebral level. Intermuscular adipose tissue (IMAT) was quantified exclusively within the erector spinae muscle and is therefore reported as a surrogate marker of trunk muscle quality rather than whole-muscle myosteatosis. Frailty was assessed with the Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS), handgrip strength and the Timed Up and Go (TUG) test. Because functional testing was incomplete, effective sample sizes varied ( n = 21-53) and are reported for every model. Results In the total cohort, a higher IMAT Index was associated with lower handgrip strength ( ρ = -0.434, p = 0.004, n = 43) and remained independent after adjustment for age, sex, BMI and ASA status (B = -1.808, 95% CI -2.994 to -0.622, p = 0.004, n = 42). Its association with the CFS was borderline univariately ( ρ = 0.273, p = 0.051, n = 52) and absent after adjustment ( p = 0.184, n = 51). Neither index was independently associated with TUG performance ( p = 0.134 and p = 0.071, n = 25). In an exploratory sex-stratified analysis, the IMAT Index correlated with the CFS in women ( ρ = 0.727, p < 0.001, n = 19) but not in men. Because the female subgroup was small ( n = 20), no sex-stratified regression or interaction test was performed. Conclusions In this small, retrospective, cross-sectional cohort, an erector-spinae-based IMAT Index was associated with handgrip strength but not independently with global clinical frailty. Automated opportunistic CT analysis may therefore identify specific muscle weakness rather than global frailty. The observed sex differences are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger, adequately powered longitudinal studies.

title: Endoscopic intervention is associated with a lower risk of in-hospital mortality in patients with acute myocardial infarction complicated by gastrointestinal bleeding.
abstract: Introduction It remains unclear whether endoscopic intervention affects the prognosis of patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) complicated by gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB). This study aimed to evaluate the association between endoscopic intervention and the risk of in-hospital all-cause mortality in patients with AMI complicated by GIB. Methods The study had a single-center retrospective cohort design and included consecutive adult patients with AMI complicated by GIB who were hospitalized at Beijing Anzhen Hospital between January 2020 and February 2026. The patients were divided into an endoscopic intervention group and a no-endoscopic intervention group according to whether or not they underwent endoscopic intervention during hospitalization. Baseline differences between the two groups were further addressed using propensity score methods. The primary outcome was in-hospital all-cause mortality. For the primary survival analysis, follow-up began at recognition of GIB, and endoscopic intervention was modeled as a time-varying exposure in Cox regression. Propensity score matching (PSM) was used as a sensitivity analysis to address measured baseline confounding. The secondary outcome was serious in-hospital clinical adverse events after GIB. Results A total of 155 hospitalized patients with AMI complicated by GIB were included in the study (endoscopy group, n = 57; non-endoscopy group, n = 98). In the adjusted time-varying Cox regression model using the recorded intraday times, endoscopic intervention was associated with a lower risk of in-hospital all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio 0.478, 95% confidence interval 0.240-0.951, P = 0.035). In the adjusted 24-hour landmark analysis, the association was directionally similar but did not reach statistical significance (hazard ratio 0.433, 95% confidence interval 0.184-1.020, P = 0.056). In the propensity-score-matched cohort, endoscopic intervention remained associated with a lower risk of in-hospital all-cause mortality after further adjustment for residual imbalance (adjusted hazard ratio 0.346, 95% confidence interval 0.152-0.786, P = 0.011). No statistically significant between-group difference was observed in serious in-hospital clinical adverse events after GIB (odds ratio 1.340, 95% confidence interval 0.660-2.724, P = 0.406). Discussion In this retrospective cohort, endoscopic intervention was associated with a lower risk of in-hospital all-cause mortality in patients with AMI complicated by GIB, although residual confounding and the uncertainty observed across complementary analyses should be considered when interpreting this association.

title: Case Report: Delayed hemobilia caused by hepatic artery pseudoaneurysm with arterio-biliary fistula after liver transplantation.
abstract: Background Hepatic artery pseudoaneurysm (HAP) is a rare but life-threatening complication following liver transplantation (LT). The formation of an arterio-biliary fistula leading to hemobilia is exceptionally uncommon, particularly when manifesting several months post-transplantation. Diagnosis and therapeutic management remain highly challenging because achieving definitive hemostasis often conflicts with the critical need to preserve graft arterial perfusion. Case presentation A 23-year-old male presented with recurrent hematemesis, hematochezia, and right upper quadrant pain 4 months after undergoing orthotopic LT for end-stage alcohol-related cirrhosis. While initial endoscopy pointed toward a duodenal bulb ulcer, a repeat endoscopic evaluation revealed fresh blood actively emerging from the major duodenal papilla, raising strong suspicion for hemobilia. Subsequent digital subtraction angiography (DSA) demonstrated a post-transplant HAP arising from the hilar hepatic arterial segment, communicating directly with the common bile duct, confirming an arterio-biliary fistula. Two sessions of transcatheter coil embolization achieved only temporary hemostasis. Following an early recurrence of bleeding, the patient underwent emergency surgery. The lesion was identified on the left hepatic artery near the porta hepatis. The surgical intervention included pseudoaneurysm resection, end-to-end hepatic artery reconstruction, and a Roux-en-Y biliary-enteric anastomosis. Despite an initially stable early postoperative course, the patient suffered a sudden circulatory collapse on postoperative day 6 and died despite aggressive resuscitation. Conclusions Hemobilia should be considered in liver transplant recipients with recurrent or unexplained gastrointestinal bleeding, particularly when blood is observed emerging from the major duodenal papilla. DSA should be performed promptly when clinical suspicion remains high, even if post-embolization CTA is inconclusive. Recurrent bleeding after embolization may indicate persistent fistulous communication and should prompt early multidisciplinary reassessment of definitive treatment options.

title: Case Report: Synchronous double primary male breast cancer and non-small cell lung cancer: diagnostic confirmation and multidisciplinary management.
abstract: Background Male breast cancer (MBC) is rare, accounting for approximately 1% of all breast cancers. When MBC is diagnosed simultaneously with a second primary lung cancer, treatment planning becomes particularly complex because diagnostic certainty, technical resectability, competing treatment windows, and radiotherapy safety must all be considered. Case presentation We report a 72-year-old man who was synchronously diagnosed with left invasive ductal breast carcinoma and right lower lobe poorly differentiated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The breast cancer was staged as pT 3 N 2a M 0 , AJCC 8th edition stage IIIA, with strong ER/PR expression and HER2 nonamplification. The lung lesion was pathologically diagnosed as poorly differentiated NSCLC without definitive glandular, squamous, or neuroendocrine differentiation and was staged as cT 3 N 0 M 0 , AJCC 8th edition stage IIB. Although stage IIB NSCLC is usually evaluated for surgery, this tumor closely involved the right lower lobe pulmonary vessels and bronchial structures, and thoracic surgeons considered upfront radical resection technically unsafe because of the risks of hemorrhage, extended resection, impaired blood supply to the remaining lobes, and loss of pulmonary function. After multidisciplinary team (MDT) discussion, the patient underwent left modified radical mastectomy, adjuvant AC-T chemotherapy, and simultaneous postmastectomy radiotherapy to the left chest wall/regional nodes with definitive radiotherapy to the right lung lesion plus concurrent cisplatin. Imaging shortly after radiotherapy showed marked shrinkage of the right lung lesion, but subsequent CT and liver MRI suggested systemic progression with multiple hepatic lesions. The patient declined liver biopsy, received one cycle of vinorelbine plus cisplatin with Endostar, discontinued further treatment, and died of liver failure in March 2026. Conclusion This case illustrates that therapeutic prioritization in synchronous double primary cancers should not be determined solely by TNM stage or chronological order of diagnosis. Instead, treatment decisions should integrate pathological distinction, tumor biology, anatomical treatability, technical resectability, curative potential, competing treatment windows, and short-term clinical threat. In selected patients, simultaneous postmastectomy radiotherapy and definitive lung radiotherapy may be feasible when supported by MDT consensus, dosimetric review, and close toxicity monitoring.

title: Reconstruction-aware radiomics for risk stratification of subsolid pulmonary nodules: technical evidence, clinical limits, and translation priorities.
abstract: Subsolid pulmonary nodules (SSNs), including pure ground-glass nodules (pGGNs) and part-solid nodules (PSNs), span transient inflammatory abnormalities and adenocarcinoma-spectrum lesions with widely different management implications. This critical narrative review treats CT reconstruction as part of the quantitative biomarker definition and asks whether targeted or high-spatial-resolution reconstruction provides stable, task-specific information beyond standardized thin-section CT. Evidence was synthesized across direct SSN reconstruction-domain studies, technical robustness studies, and clinical prediction studies. Direct imaging studies support improved depiction of selected fine structures, while same-scan GGN evidence demonstrates substantial pixel-size dependence of radiomic features and model composition. However, most clinical models were not evaluated in paired reconstruction domains, external validation with calibration remains uncommon, and no prospective study demonstrating management or patient benefit from reconstruction-aware radiomics in SSNs was identified in the literature reviewed. Persistent pGGNs provide a biological and technical rationale for investigating incremental quantitative information, but greater benefit than in PSNs has not been demonstrated. In PSNs, any model must add value beyond solid-component measurements, consolidation-to-tumor ratio, morphology, and longitudinal growth. Translation therefore requires reconstruction and segmentation robustness testing, strong conventional comparators, external calibration, prespecified thresholds, and prospective decision-linked evaluation. Until such benefit and safety are demonstrated, reconstruction-aware radiomics should remain investigational or confined to governed, domain-checked decision-support pathways.

title: FroHyNet: frozen temporal priors and trainable hypergraph fusion for brain time-series classification.
abstract: Background Functional brain time-series classification is constrained by small clinical cohorts. Handcrafted features are sample-efficient but discard temporal detail; end-to-end networks must estimate many temporal parameters from limited labels; and frozen time-series foundation models reduce that estimation burden but typically encode each channel independently, leaving coordinated activity across brain regions unmodeled. Methods We introduce the Frozen Temporal-Hypergraph Network (FroHyNet), an asymmetric parallel framework that preserves channel-wise temporal representations from a frozen MantisV2 encoder while a trainable spatio-temporal hypergraph branch learns topology-aware spatial corrections. Bottleneck-mix Top-K (BM-TopK) then residual-injects these corrections only along selected channel and latent-feature axes, treating the spatial stream as a selective update rather than a dense overwrite of the temporal representation. We conduct five-fold cross-validation across two functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) and three functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) datasets. Results FroHyNet achieves the best average accuracy and area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUC) among methods evaluated on all five datasets, while keeping the trainable-parameter count well below those of from-scratch temporal networks. Gains are concentrated on fNIRS, with more modest improvements on the smaller fMRI cohorts. Branch ablations indicate dataset-dependent complementarity between the two streams, and fusion ablations on HC-D favor BM-TopK over the evaluated dense and recurrent alternatives.

title: Contrast-enhanced ultrasound-assisted catheter drainage for paravertebral tuberculous abscesses: a retrospective study of procedural safety.
abstract: Background Paravertebral tuberculous abscess is a clinically important complication of spinal tuberculosis and may require image-guided drainage before definitive surgical management. Contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) may improve visualization of abscess vascularity and internal architecture, but its clinical value in catheter drainage for paravertebral tuberculous abscess remains insufficiently defined. Methods This retrospective historical-control study included 67 patients with lumbar spinal tuberculosis complicated by paravertebral tuberculous abscess who underwent ultrasound-guided catheter drainage at Hangzhou Red Cross Hospital between January 2010 and January 2025. Patients were divided into a conventional ultrasound-guided drainage group (Group A, n = 39) and a CEUS-assisted drainage group (Group B, n = 28). Baseline characteristics, postoperative recovery parameters, inflammatory markers, pain scores, clinical outcomes, and drainage-related complications were compared between groups. Results Postprocedural bleeding occurred after 5 of 41 drainage procedures (12.20%) in the conventional ultrasound-guided group and after 0 of 31 procedures (0.00%) in the CEUS-assisted group. Catheter occlusion and pericatheter purulent discharge rates did not differ between groups. Operative time, length of hospital stay, intraoperative blood loss, inflammatory markers, pain scores, cure rate, and recurrence rate also did not differ between groups. Conclusions In this retrospective historical cohort, CEUS-assisted drainage was associated with fewer recorded postprocedural bleeding events and provided additional anatomical information for procedural planning.

title: High-frequency ultrasound-derived imaging biomarkers in inflammatory skin diseases.
abstract: Background Inflammatory skin diseases produce structural, vascular, and tissue-remodeling changes that may extend beyond abnormalities detectable by clinical examination. High-frequency ultrasound (HFUS), including ultra-high-frequency systems, provides noninvasive, real-time assessment of cutaneous morphology and inflammatory vascular activity. Objective To examine HFUS in inflammatory skin diseases from an imaging biomarker perspective, emphasizing measurable structural, vascular, and mechanical features and their potential clinical applications. Key findings Candidate ultrasound biomarkers include epidermal and dermal thickness, echogenicity, tissue interfaces, perifollicular abnormalities, fluid collections, fibrosis, architectural distortion, Doppler-detected vascularity, and tissue stiffness. Their clinical relevance is particularly evident in psoriasis, atopic dermatitis, acne vulgaris, hidradenitis suppurativa, and morphea, with emerging applications in other inflammatory dermatoses. In selected disorders, HFUS may reveal clinically occult abnormalities, while treatment-associated changes in selected parameters support their potential as candidate treatment-response biomarkers. Quantitative image analysis, elastography, and artificial intelligence may further improve reproducibility and interpretation. Conclusions HFUS is evolving from predominantly morphological imaging toward a platform for deriving imaging biomarkers in inflammatory skin disease. Broader clinical implementation will require standardized acquisition, validated biomarkers and thresholds, operator training, and prospective evidence demonstrating clinical utility.

Their clinical relevance is particularly evident in psoriasis, atopic dermatitis, acne vulgaris, hidradenitis suppurativa, and morphea, with emerging applications in other inflammatory dermatoses. In selected disorders, HFUS may reveal clinically occult abnormalities, while treatment-associated changes in selected parameters support their potential as candidate treatment-response biomarkers. Quantitative image analysis, elastography, and artificial intelligence may further improve reproducibility and interpretation.

Conclusions

HFUS is evolving from predominantly morphological imaging toward a platform for deriving imaging biomarkers in inflammatory skin disease. Broader clinical implementation will require standardized acquisition, validated biomarkers and thresholds, operator training, and prospective evidence demonstrating clinical utility.

title: Beyond overall accuracy: subgroup performance and threshold calibration of AI-assisted chest radiography for equity-oriented pulmonary tuberculosis screening.
abstract: Artificial intelligence-assisted computer-aided detection (CAD) can expand access to chest radiography interpretation for pulmonary tuberculosis screening and triage, but high overall discrimination does not ensure safety at a deployed threshold. This focused narrative Mini Review synthesizes evidence on subgroup performance, threshold calibration, external validity, and implementation of CAD for adult pulmonary tuberculosis. Smear-negative, asymptomatic, and some HIV-associated disease may be less radiographically visible, increasing false-negative risk. Conversely, previous tuberculosis and competing chronic abnormalities reduce specificity and concentrate unnecessary confirmatory testing. Sex, age, geography, clinical setting, verification design, and software version can further alter operating performance. A numerical threshold is therefore not a portable algorithm property but a context-specific clinical resource-allocation policy. We propose a lifecycle in which programs define the intended use, lock the product and version, conduct representative local validation, select an operating point under explicit sensitivity and capacity constraints, audit clinically relevant subgroups, and monitor the complete care pathway. Stratified thresholds and multivariable models may improve selected settings, but current evidence does not justify replacing robust local calibration and governance. Prospective evaluations should compare threshold strategies under common verification standards and report missed cases, referral burden, treatment initiation, and patient-important outcomes.

title: Thyroid-bed schwannoma mimicking a thyroid neoplasm: a case report.
abstract: Intrathyroidal schwannomas are rare, and thyroid-bed schwannomas are scarcer, with merely a few case reports and tough preoperative differentiation. We report a 33-year-old female with a swallowing-movable left neck mass and normal thyroid function. Gray-scale B-mode ultrasound, color Doppler flow imaging and contrast-enhanced ultrasound showed showed a heterogeneously enhanced TI-RADS 3 lesion preoperatively suspected as a follicular neoplasm. Fine-needle aspiration (FNA) biopsy was performed, which failed to yield a definitive pathological diagnosis and yielded Bethesda category I. She received left lobectomy plus isthmectomy, and pathology confirmed thyroid-bed schwannoma sparing thyroid parenchyma; she recovered well with normal thyroid function postoperatively. Due to its low incidence, this tumor is often mistaken for an intrathyroidal nodule on ultrasound. Total surgical excision is the first-line therapy with good overall prognosis. Unlike intrathyroidal schwannomas, most thyroid-bed lesions can be enucleated alone without routine thyroidectomy; hemithyroidectomy is needed for dense adhesion, and total thyroidectomy is rarely required. Considering the low diagnostic value of FNA, multidisciplinary consultation of pathology, radiology and surgery is advised for lesions with atypical imaging, inconclusive FNA or ill-defined thyroid margins. Ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy (CNB) should be performed if needed to tailor proper treatment.

title: Concurrent Bartholin gland and perianal abscesses in a woman: a case report of a diagnostic challenge.
abstract: Background Bartholin gland abscess and perianal abscess are common suppurative infections involving anatomically adjacent regions of the female perineum. Because both conditions may present with localized pain and swelling, distinguishing their respective origins and determining the extent of infection can be challenging. The concomitant occurrence of these two abscesses is uncommon, and its diagnostic and therapeutic considerations remain poorly characterized. We report a rare case of concomitant Bartholin gland and perianal abscesses and describe the diagnostic process and multidisciplinary surgical management. Case presentation An 18-year-old woman presented with progressive perineal and perianal pain and swelling. Pelvic computed tomography demonstrated abscess formation involving the perianal and left perineal soft tissues, and a possible communication between the two lesions was initially suspected. Emergency surgery was performed. The perianal abscess was incised and drained, and an infected anal gland was identified and excised, with bridge drainage established between the drainage incisions. Intraoperative exploration revealed no communication between the perianal abscess and the adjacent perineal lesion. Following gynecological consultation, the separate left vulvar abscess was drained and treated with Jacobi ring fistulization. Culture of the perineal abscess grew Escherichia coli, whereas the perianal abscess culture showed no bacterial growth. Follow-up magnetic resonance imaging 1 month after surgery demonstrated a cystic lesion in the anatomical region of the left Bartholin gland, supporting the Bartholin gland origin of the previously drained perineal abscess. The patient showed satisfactory clinical recovery, with complete healing of the perianal and perineal wounds at 4 months and no evidence of recurrent abscess during the available follow-up. Conclusion Concomitant Bartholin gland and perianal abscesses may be difficult to distinguish because of their overlapping clinical manifestations and anatomical proximity. Clinicians should consider the possibility of multiple independent or potentially related infectious foci and systematically evaluate adjacent anatomical regions. Careful physical examination, appropriate imaging, intraoperative assessment, and timely multidisciplinary collaboration can facilitate accurate diagnosis and individualized surgical management.
