title: CuFormer U-Net: a transformer-enhanced multi-task network for cucumber leaf disease detection and segmentation.
abstract: Cucumber foliar symptoms reduce functional leaf area and complicate greenhouse scouting. This study presents CuFormer U-Net, a Transformer-enhanced multi-task network for three-class image-level classification on the 3,754-image Kaggle benchmark (healthy, powdery mildew, and downy mildew) and binary visible-symptom segmentation on a separate 400-image greenhouse cohort (200 healthy and 200 affected leaves). The greenhouse annotations comprise 2,705 rectangles (1,741 color-abnormality and 964 tissue-damage instances); rectangle-seeded lesion masks were manually refined for the dense-prediction experiments. The reported fixed-split point estimates were 96.7% accuracy, 96.3% macro precision, 95.8% macro recall, and 96.0% macro F1 for classification, and 92.4% mean image-wise Dice, 83.1% macro IoU, 93.2% foreground precision, and 91.7% foreground recall for segmentation. The complete internal-validation ablation configuration reached 93.1% Dice and 87.3% IoU. The available experiment archive does not contain independent-seed reruns, per-image predictions for inferential testing, annotator-level masks, quantitative results for the separate 100-image greenhouse stress-test cohort, or reproducible hardware profiling. Accordingly, all between-model differences are interpreted descriptively, the external cohort is not presented as formal external validation, and robustness and deployment claims have been moderated. CuFormer U-Net provides a technically motivated basis for joint recognition and spatial characterization, but confirmatory multi-run and multi-site evaluation is required. boundary refinement, cucumber leaf disease, multi-task learning, plant disease, precision agriculture, semantic segmentation, vision transformer.

title: Comprehensive artificial intelligence-assisted mental health program for university students in China (CAMPUS): study protocol for a multi-center prospective cohort with planned embedded randomized intervention trials.
abstract: University students face a rising prevalence of depression, anxiety, insomnia, and suicidal ideation that exceeds the capacity of conventional, resource-constrained campus support services. Although artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted screening tools have emerged, many have evaluated selected modalities or isolated prediction tasks, and their integration with prospectively evaluated intervention pathways remains limited. This protocol describes the Comprehensive Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Mental Health Program for University Students in China (CAMPUS), a multi-center research program comprising a five-year prospective cohort, eight planned embedded randomized controlled trials, and exploratory multimodal AI and multi-omics studies across seven Chinese universities. Longitudinal cohort enrolment commenced at Henan Medical University in September 2025 and is planned to expand across seven participating universities. Multidimensional screening integrates psychological self-report (PHQ-9, GAD-7, ISI, BSI-CV, and others), physiological measurements (EEG, MRI, fNIRS, HRV, eye tracking, facial-expression analysis, ERP, voice acoustics), and an exploratory biospecimen component for multi-omics profiling, potentially including genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic, and microbiome analyses, subject to the finalization and approval of layer-specific protocols. Students identified through cohort screening as potentially eligible for an intervention trial will undergo trial-specific eligibility assessment. Those who meet the eligibility criteria and provide trial-specific informed consent will be individually randomized in a 1:1 ratio to the intervention or its comparator within one of eight separate two-arm, multi-center, parallel-group randomized controlled trials. A Transformer-based multimodal AI framework with SHAP-based feature attribution will be developed and internally evaluated for questionnaire-defined risk stratification and exploratory treatment-response prediction. The initial Henan Medical University cohort recruitment and university-student mental-health assessment were approved by the Ethics Review Committee of Henan Medical University (XYLL-20250484), and written informed consent is obtained from participants before enrolment. Each additional participating center will obtain local ethics approval before study activation. Findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications, scientific conferences, and policy briefs, providing evidence that may inform the design and prospective evaluation of youth mental-health programs in other university settings. Clinical trial registration The two clinical trials were registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR). The registration details and URLs are as follows: ChiCTR2500113527: https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=298271; ChiCTR2500113613: https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=298268.

title: Deep learning prediction of overall survival in glioblastoma patients using pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI and clinical data.
abstract: Purpose Glioblastoma (GBM) exhibits variable treatment response and patients shown a median survival of 15 months. A major challenge lies in the difficulty of reliably assessing treatment response at an early stage, as it can usually only be evaluated on anatomical MRI performed up to three months after the start of treatment, when early interpretation may be complicated by the risk of pseudoprogression. Accurately predicting short-term and long-term survivors before radiotherapy and chemotherapy is therefore crucial. The objective of this study is to develop an AI model designed to predict survival outcomes based exclusively on pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI and clinical data. Material and methods A total of 1,575 retrospective T1-Gd brain images were obtained from 175 patients treated for GBM between 2018 and 2023. A ResNet-51Q model pretrained on ImageNet was fine-tuned on pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI using transfer learning. To incorporate clinical data, deep hybrid learning (DHL) models were trained. Results At patient-level, the AI model achieved 81.08% (CI 95%: 67.57-91.89), 68.42% (CI 95%: 47.06-88.89) and 94.44% (CI 95%: 81.82-1.00) for accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity, respectively, for the classification of short-term and long-term survivors using only pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI. At patient-level, the three-class model using only pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI, achieved 87.18% (CI 95%: 76.92- 97.44), 87.18% (CI 95%: 76.68-96.97), and 93.59% (CI 95%: 88.03-98.41) for accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity, respectively. In comparison at slice-level, the three-class model using only pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI, achieved 81.77% (CI 95%: 70.66-91.45), 81.77% (CI 95%: 71.07-91.33), and 90.88% (CI 95%: 85.25-95.74) for accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity, respectively. In comparison the DHL model with clinical data achieved an accuracy of 84.62% (CI 95%: 71.79-94.87), a sensitivity of 84.62% (CI 95%: 72.54-95.24) and a specificity of 92.31% (CI 95%: 86.07-97.53) and 76.32% (CI 95%: 63.16-89.47), 76.11% (CI 95%: 61.63-88.75) and 92.06% (CI 95%: 87.51-96.23) for four overall survival classification. For multiclass tasks, metrics were calculated using a macro-averaged approach. Conclusion The combination of pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI and clinical data using the DHL model for early survival prediction; however, adding clinical variables yielded comparable prognostic performance rather than a demonstrable enhancement over imaging features alone. The use of AI models to predict survival outcome in GBM from pre-chemoradiotherapy data may support pre-chemoradiotherapy prognostic stratification.

title: Q-rung orthopair fuzzy framework for multimodal MRI image fusion and U-Net-based segmentation for brain tumor detection.
abstract: Medical image analysis is a significant research domain in contemporary healthcare systems, which helps to accurately diagnose diseases and support clinical decision-making. This domain consists of important operations, including image enhancement, fusion, segmentation, morphological processing, and denoising, which assist in the effective understanding of complex biomedical information. Multimodal image fusion and segmentation are particularly important among these processes, as they enable the integration of complementary diagnostic information and the clear interpretation of clinically meaningful structures. However, medical images often consist of uncertainty, noise, and incomplete pixel information, creating major challenges for conventional analytical techniques. To address these challenges, the present study introduces a q-rung orthopair fuzzy set (qROFS)-based framework for multimodal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) fusion, subsequently a U-Net-based segmentation architecture for brain tumor detection. To effectively handle uncertainty and preserve important image information, the fusion strategy is designed based on q-rung orthopair fuzzy Hamacher t-norm and t-conorm operators to integrate complementary information in four different MRI modalities, including T1, T1ce, T2, and Flair. The resultant fused images are subsequently processed through a U-Net architecture to obtain precise tumor segmentation. Experiments conducted on the BraTS 2020 benchmark dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework. Across the four MRI modalities (T1, T1ce, T2, and Flair), the proposed fusion framework attains the best quantitative performance when compared to state-of-the-art methods with an SSIM of 0.9271, an MSSIM of 0.9481, a PSNR of 24.7130 dB, a low AMBE of 6.6779, a Correlation coefficient of 0.9583, an MI of 1.4097, and a UQI of 0.9767. A comparative evaluation with existing fuzzy set-based fusion models further assures the effectiveness of the proposed qROFS-based framework for multimodal MRI image fusion. Furthermore, the U-Net-based segmentation model achieves excellent performance, with an accuracy of 98.96%, a precision of 98.95%, a sensitivity of 98.94%, and a specificity of 99.65%.

title: Prospective validation of multimodal risk stratification using clinical and quantitative imaging features for 12-month outcomes after minimally invasive surgery for lumbar disc herniation.
abstract: Background Lumbar disc herniation (LDH) is a common spinal disorder leading to chronic low back pain and radiating leg pain. Minimally invasive surgery is the preferred treatment, but postoperative recovery varies significantly, making accurate preoperative prognosis prediction a challenge. Methods This study developed and prospectively validated a multimodal risk-stratification framework integrating structured clinical variables, conventional imaging parameters, CT/MRI radiomics, and high-dimensional image-derived features. A total of 773 patients were analyzed, including 665 patients in the retrospective development cohort and 108 patients in an independent prospective validation cohort. The retrospective cohort was divided into a training cohort ( n = 532) and an internal validation cohort ( n = 133). Feature selection, parameter optimization, and classification-threshold determination were performed exclusively within the training cohort, and the finalized framework was subsequently evaluated in the internal and prospective validation cohorts. Results The integrated multimodal approach achieved an ROC-AUC of 0.937 (95% CI, 0.900-0.975) and a PR-AUC of 0.849 in the internal validation cohort, and an ROC-AUC of 0.976 (95% CI, 0.951-1.000) and a PR-AUC of 0.941 in the prospective validation cohort. Its discrimination was comparable to that achieved using structured clinical and conventional imaging information alone and was higher than that of isolated quantitative imaging approaches. At the prespecified training-derived classification threshold of 0.318, sensitivity, specificity, and balanced accuracy in the prospective cohort were 85.3%, 95.9%, and 90.6%, respectively. Calibration analysis demonstrated residual probability miscalibration despite strong discrimination, although training-derived logistic recalibration improved the Brier score. Conclusion Multimodal integration of clinical and quantitative imaging information demonstrated strong discrimination for 12-month postoperative outcome stratification in both internal and prospective validation cohorts. However, the incremental discriminative value beyond structured clinical and conventional imaging information was limited, and residual miscalibration remained in the prospective cohort. Further multicenter validation, standardized quantitative imaging workflows, and calibration assessment are warranted before clinical translation.
originalAbstract:
Background

Lumbar disc herniation (LDH) is a common spinal disorder leading to chronic low back pain and radiating leg pain. Minimally invasive surgery is the preferred treatment, but postoperative recovery varies significantly, making accurate preoperative prognosis prediction a challenge.

Methods

This study developed and prospectively validated a multimodal risk-stratification framework integrating structured clinical variables, conventional imaging parameters, CT/MRI radiomics, and high-dimensional image-derived features. A total of 773 patients were analyzed, including 665 patients in the retrospective development cohort and 108 patients in an independent prospective validation cohort. The retrospective cohort was divided into a training cohort (n = 532) and an internal validation cohort (n = 133). Feature selection, parameter optimization, and classification-threshold determination were performed exclusively within the training cohort, and the finalized framework was subsequently evaluated in the internal and prospective validation cohorts.

Results

The integrated multimodal approach achieved an ROC-AUC of 0.937 (95% CI, 0.900-0.975) and a PR-AUC of 0.849 in the internal validation cohort, and an ROC-AUC of 0.976 (95% CI, 0.951-1.000) and a PR-AUC of 0.941 in the prospective validation cohort. Its discrimination was comparable to that achieved using structured clinical and conventional imaging information alone and was higher than that of isolated quantitative imaging approaches. At the prespecified training-derived classification threshold of 0.318, sensitivity, specificity, and balanced accuracy in the prospective cohort were 85.3%, 95.9%, and 90.6%, respectively. Calibration analysis demonstrated residual probability miscalibration despite strong discrimination, although training-derived logistic recalibration improved the Brier score.

Conclusion

Multimodal integration of clinical and quantitative imaging information demonstrated strong discrimination for 12-month postoperative outcome stratification in both internal and prospective validation cohorts. However, the incremental discriminative value beyond structured clinical and conventional imaging information was limited, and residual miscalibration remained in the prospective cohort. Further multicenter validation, standardized quantitative imaging workflows, and calibration assessment are warranted before clinical translation.

title: Temporal phase coverage and patient cohort size in deep learning-based cardiac cine computed tomography angiography segmentation.
abstract: Background Annotating all phases of cine computed tomography angiography (CTA) is burdensome. We evaluated how temporal phase coverage and patient cohort size affect deep learning-based cardiac segmentation. Methods Twelve 3D U-Net models were trained using a 110-patient single-phase CTA dataset or a 20-patient, 20-phase cine CTA dataset. Phase-coverage ablations used one, two, or 20 phases; patient-count ablations were performed within both datasets. One cine patient was used for validation and four independent patients were used for testing. Five cardiac structures were evaluated using Dice and the 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95). Phase-wise and patient-level Dice consistency and structure-specific volumetric variability within and between subjects were assessed. Results Full cine training produced higher overall Dice (0.89 vs. 0.87) and lower overall HD95 (4.87 vs. 9.78 mm) than the single-phase reference (both p < 0.05). Right ventricular (RV) Dice was higher (0.91 vs. 0.84) and HD95 was lower (5.16 vs. 22.75 mm; both p < 0.05). The two-phase model achieved an overall Dice of 0.88 and an overall HD95 of 7.85 mm; neither metric differed significantly from the single-phase reference. HD95 generally increased with smaller cohorts, and both metrics deteriorated markedly in the five-patient configurations. Full cine training showed flatter phase-wise Dice profiles and lower across-phase variability. Between-subject volume differences exceeded phase-related within-subject differences for all structures (all p < 0.05). Conclusion In this cross-cohort comparison, full cine training showed higher overall Dice, lower overall HD95, and greater phase-wise consistency than single-phase training. The evaluated two-phase configuration may inform annotation-efficient cine CTA dataset design, but broader validation is needed.

title: Automated Nuchal Translucency analysis for early prenatal risk stratification.
abstract: Nuchal Translucency (NT) is a measurement taken from ultrasound images described as the gathering of fluid behind the fetus's neck, during 11-13 weeks. Increased Nuchal Translucency can lead to high risk of chromosomal abnormalities like Down Syndrome. The existing AI model may struggle to detect the subtle difference due to low resolution fetal movement, which can lead to errors in measurements and diagnosis. In addition, traditional NT measurement methods rely heavily on manual caliper placement, making the process operator-dependent and reducing consistency and automation. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an Enhanced Multi-Scale Spatial Temporal Graph Attention Network (EMSSTGAN) to predict the risk of chromosomal abnormalities in NT. Initially, the input images of NT are pre-processed using feature refinement attention network (FRANet) for denoising and Multi-Scale Attention Retinex Network (MARN) for contrast enhancement. NT detection is then performed by localizing the nuchal translucency region using bounding box annotations, followed by U-Net-based segmentation for precise extraction of the NT area. The Active Contour Model (ACM) is subsequently applied to measure the NT thickness based on boundary geometry. The thickness when compared with threshold values is used to identify the risk of chromosomal abnormalities as low, medium and high. The proposed model achieves an accuracy of 98.15%, an error of 1.85%, and a FDR of 2.44%, respectively.

title: Diffusion-augmented contrastive learning for diabetic retinopathy severity classification.
abstract: Automated diabetic retinopathy (DR) severity classification faces persistent challenges from limited annotated datasets, severe class imbalance across the five-level International Clinical Diabetic Retinopathy (ICDR) scale, and domain shift between imaging environments. This paper presents an integrated deep learning framework that extends our earlier Fused Ensemble Convolutional Inception Network (93.2% accuracy) through three complementary innovations. First, a class-conditional latent denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) generates anatomically realistic synthetic fundus images for underrepresented DR severity levels, addressing data scarcity and class imbalance simultaneously. Second, a SimCLR contrastive self-supervised pre-training protocol, applied to the combined real-and-synthetic corpus, learns discriminative retinal representations prior to supervised fine-tuning. Third, a five-model ensemble (EfficientNet-B3, ResNet-50, VGG16, VGG19, and DenseNet-121) fused via a learned Pattern-Net achieves improved generalization through architectural diversity. Evaluated on the APTOS 2019 dataset under 5-fold stratified cross-validation, the integrated framework achieves 95.1% accuracy, 0.928 quadratic weighted kappa (QWK), 0.91 F1-score, and 0.97 AUC. Class-wise improvements over the EfficientNet-B3 baseline reach +23.8 percentage points for Severe DR (61.8 → 85.6%) and +17.7 for Mild DR (71.2 → 88.9%). Independent zero-shot validation on EyePACS yields 78.4% accuracy, 0.809 QWK, 0.738 macro F1, and 0.887 macro AUC, quantifying the expected performance reduction under domain shift. Fold-level variability and paired out-of-fold statistical analyses are additionally reported, and Grad-CAM visualization is included for qualitative model interpretability. These results demonstrate the synergistic benefit of generative augmentation with self-supervised representation learning for imbalanced medical image classification, with implications for scalable automated DR screening in resource-limited settings.

title: Mammography datasets and artificial intelligence for breast cancer detection: challenges, bias, and future directions.
abstract: Background Breast cancer is still one of the main causes of death in women from cancer worldwide, and early detection is crucial. Mammography is the primary imaging modality for breast cancer screening and recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have significantly enhanced automated breast cancer detection. This review takes a data-centered approach, examining key characteristics of public datasets, the contributions of mammography data to AI for breast cancer detection, and the implications for clinical generalizability. This review, however, takes a data-centered approach, critically analyzing characteristics of publicly available mammography datasets, and the role of mammography data to the development, performance and clinical generalization of AI models for the detection of breast cancer. The datasets are compared on the following aspects: dataset size, quality of the annotations, imaging modality, clinical metadata, dataset accessibility and demographic diversity. Analysis reveals that the quality, diversity and representativeness of the data used are critical for the performance and generalizability of AI models, ranging from the traditional machine learning era to the current era of deep learning, transformer-based systems, multimodal learning, explainable AI and privacy-preserving learning. Conclusion The results show that, apart from the development of AI model architectures, it is a necessity to have standardized, diverse and clinically representative datasets to make further progress in AI-assisted mammography. The review emphasizes the importance of establishing a comprehensive benchmark dataset for mammography that is large and diverse to enhance reproducibility, to fairly evaluate models, and to develop strong, clinically viable AI systems for breast cancer detection.

title: Beyond diagnostic accuracy: navigating the artificial intelligence data tsunami toward value-based implementation in gastroenterology.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) in gastrointestinal (GI) endoscopy has evolved from its early application in simple edge detection to highly sophisticated technologies designed to improve detection of neoplastic and preneoplastic lesions and support clinical decision-making. However, this rapid technological evolution has generated a " data tsunami " or " datanami ": an overwhelming and continuously expanding volume of information that, frequently, exceeds the ability of clinicians and patients to process, interpret, and apply it effectively. Substantial investments in AI have been driven by expectations of improved efficiency and reduced healthcare costs. Nevertheless, the metrics used to justify the adoption of AI-assisted diagnostic and therapeutic strategies remain inadequately standardized, leaving the true cost-effectiveness of these technologies uncertain. Current AI research in gastroenterology has primarily focused on improving diagnostic performance rather than evaluating long-term clinical outcomes or economic value. To address this limitation, investigators employ stochastic microsimulation models, which simulate individual patient trajectories and enable more robust assessments of cost-effectiveness. As the field progresses from AI to extended intelligence and, ultimately, intelligent assistance, the role of humans becomes increasingly central. Rather than replacing clinical judgment, AI should augment human expertise, with healthcare professionals serving as the critical link between technological innovation and meaningful clinical benefit. This review examines whether AI applications in GI diseases can be implemented cost-effectively in routine clinical practice for diagnosis and treatment. It further explores the indispensable human dimension of AI adoption, emphasizing accountability, reliability, ethical oversight, and responsible implementation as essential safeguards for current and future clinical applications.

title: Segmentation of ovarian cancer tumors from CT images based on a two-stage neural network fusion system.
abstract: The detection of ovarian cancer using computed tomography images is making rapid progress, combining the strengths of different neural networks within a complex ensemble, a more effective model can be created to support medical decision-making in ovarian cancer cases. Various neural networks and ensemble models were tested on the TCGA OV database. Tumor regions were segmented using computer-assisted annotation masks, while molecular subtype labels were assigned at the patient level based on TCGA genomic classifications and mapped to tumors. As the main novelty, the proposed method involves a two-stage fusion system. The first stage combines several neural networks into four ensembles to capture diverse features, and the second stage integrates these results into a global system to enhance segmentation accuracy. The selected models demonstrated strong segmentation performance within the investigated experimental setting and were subsequently integrated into the proposed two-stage fusion framework. The neural networks for the first stage are Attention U-Net, DeepLabV3+, and ViT. The results show that the proposed two-stage fusion system achieved higher observed segmentation performance than the evaluated individual neural networks and first-stage ensemble configurations within the present TCGA-OV experimental setting. Across the five evaluated classes, the Global System achieved an average F1 score of 93.53%, recall of 93.38%, and precision of 93.68%, supporting the technical feasibility of the proposed two-stage fusion approach for ovarian tumor segmentation within the investigated dataset.

title: The "Sandwich" technique using a lateral locking plate and intramedullary reconstruction plate with bone cement for osteoporotic proximal humerus fractures: a case series.
abstract: Introduction Although lateral locking plate fixation is widely used for displaced proximal humerus fractures, fixation failure remains a major concern in elderly osteoporotic patients, particularly when medial column defects are present. Poor cancellous bone quality reduces screw purchase, while medial comminution and metaphyseal bone voids weaken the ability of the proximal humerus to resist varus and axial loading. Existing augmentation methods address only part of this problem. Fibular strut allografts can provide intramedullary and medial support but may be limited by graft availability, size matching, cost, and technical complexity, and they do not directly reinforce the screw-bone interface of all proximal screws. Cement augmentation can improve screw purchase, but cement alone does not create a defined intramedullary support structure or reconstruct medial column bone defects. Therefore, a composite fixation strategy is needed to simultaneously provide lateral fixation, intramedullary support, medial column stability, enhanced screw purchase, and bone defect reconstruction. To address this clinical gap, we developed the "Sandwich" technique, which combines a lateral locking plate, an intramedullary reconstruction plate, PMMA bone cement, and allogeneic cancellous bone graft to create a multidirectional support construct. Methods Five patients with osteoporotic proximal humerus fractures and medial column defects were treated using the "Sandwich" technique. This construct consisted of a lateral locking plate, an intramedullary reconstruction plate, PMMA bone cement, and allogeneic cancellous bone graft. The lateral locking plate provided lateral fixation, whereas the intramedullary reconstruction plate provided internal structural support. PMMA bone cement was placed between the two plates to reinforce screw purchase and construct stability, and allogeneic cancellous bone graft was used to fill the residual metaphyseal and medial column defects. Results The mean operative time was 123.0 ± 16.1 min, with an average blood loss of 206.0 ± 85.3 mL, hospital stay of 8.4 ± 1.1 days, and mean hospitalization cost of 56,258.4 ± 6,152.1 CNY. At 12 months postoperatively, all fractures achieved radiographic union without loss of reduction, screw penetration, or varus collapse. The mean CMS was 87.0 ± 6.0 and the mean Neer score was 86.0 ± 6.1. No cases of avascular necrosis or fixation failure were observed. Conclusion The "Sandwich" technique provides strong medial and intramedullary support, improves screw fixation, and enhances overall biomechanical stability in osteoporotic proximal humerus fractures. It achieved excellent healing and functional recovery with minimal complications, representing a promising surgical alternative to traditional fibular graft-assisted fixation.

title: Jejunal intussusception following distal gastrectomy with Billroth I anastomosis: a case report.
abstract: A 41-year-old male patient presented with acute persistent abdominal pain for 4 h and was admitted to our hospital in October 2023. The patient had a height of 178 cm and a weight of 55 kg, with a precisely calculated body mass index (BMI) of 17.4 kg/m² and a body surface area of 1.73 m². He was diagnosed with acute gastric perforation and underwent emergency distal gastrectomy combined with Billroth I gastroduodenal anastomosis and intraoperative jejunal feeding tube placement. On postoperative day (POD) 19, the patient developed aggravated abdominal distension and paroxysmal abdominal pain without fever, vomiting, or diarrhea. Laboratory tests showed slightly elevated inflammatory markers and normal serum lactate, while abdominal computed tomography (CT) revealed typical intestinal intussusception and partial intestinal obstruction. Emergency re-laparotomy confirmed antegrade jejunojejunal intussusception located approximately 20 cm distal to the Treitz ligament, with an intussusception length of approximately 40 cm. Manual reduction was successfully performed without intestinal resection or intraoperative complications. The patient achieved uneventful gastrointestinal function recovery and was discharged on POD 12 after reoperation. No recurrence of intussusception was observed during 6 months of outpatient follow-up. This study reports a rare case of late-onset antegrade jejunojejunal intussusception following Billroth I gastrectomy. Combined effects of low BMI-related loose mesentery, intra-abdominal postoperative adhesions, and indwelling jejunal feeding tube were identified as potential associative risk factors rather than definitive causal factors. We aim to summarize the clinical characteristics, diagnostic strategies, and standardized prevention and treatment protocols of this rare postoperative complication to supplement relevant clinical evidence.

title: When should a laparoscopic cholecystectomy be performed after ERCP for common bile duct stones combined with gallbladder stones? A meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
abstract: Background Gallstones combined with common bile duct stones are a common disease in biliary surgery. At present, for gallbladder stones with common bile duct stones, the globally recognized standard treatment is a step-by-step treatment of "endoscopy combined with surgery". First, more urgent and potentially life-threatening bile duct stones are treated, and then gallbladder stones are treated. However, after the common bile duct stones are successfully removed by ERCP, how long should laparoscopic cholecystectomy be performed at intervals? There is a dispute between "early" (defined as within 72 h after ERCP) and "delayed" (defined as 72 h after ERCP). The conclusion is not yet uniform. Objective To systematically analyze the efficacy and safety of early LC and delayed LC in patients with gallstones and common bile duct stones after ERCP, to provide current high-level evidence-based medical evidence for clinical decision-making, to help clinicians optimize the diagnosis and treatment process, to reduce the occurrence of adverse complications caused by treatment. Method PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, Scopus, and other databases were searched to collect randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing early LC and delayed LC after ERCP from inception to December 2025. Two reviewers independently screened literature, extracted data, and assessed the risk of bias of included studies using the Cochrane ROB evaluation tool. The RevMan 5.4 software was used to analyze the outcomes of each group. Unlike previous meta-analyses, this study only included randomized controlled trials and incorporated the latest ones. Moreover, the quality of each outcome indicator was evaluated using the GRADE method. Result This meta-analysis included 7 randomized controlled trials involving 593 patients (296 in the early LC group and 297 in the delayed LC group). Compared with the delayed LC group, the early LC group was associated with a significantly lower rate of conversion to open surgery ( RR = 0.35, 95 % CI : 0.17-0.68, P = 0.002), shorter operation time ( MD = -14.37 min, 95 % CI : -28.22 to -0.51, P = 0.04), shorter postoperative hospital stay ( MD = -0.81 days, 95 % CI : -1.20 to -0.42, P < 0.0001), and lower incidence of incision infection (RR = 0.21, 95 % CI : 0.07-0.61, P = 0.004). No significant difference was observed between the two groups in the incidence of bile leakage ( RD = -0.04, 95 % CI : -0.12-0.04, P = 0.30). Conclusion In conclusion, the available RCT evidence suggests that early LC following successful ERCP may provide clinical advantages over delayed LC, including lower conversion and infection rates and shorter operative and postoperative hospital stay. However, because of outcome-level heterogeneity, the limited number of included trials, and few bile-leakage events, these findings should be interpreted with caution and further verified in larger well-designed RCTs. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261395564, PROSPERO CRD420261395564.

At present, for gallbladder stones with common bile duct stones, the globally recognized standard treatment is a step-by-step treatment of "endoscopy combined with surgery". First, more urgent and potentially life-threatening bile duct stones are treated, and then gallbladder stones are treated. However, after the common bile duct stones are successfully removed by ERCP, how long should laparoscopic cholecystectomy be performed at intervals? There is a dispute between "early" (defined as within 72 h after ERCP) and "delayed" (defined as 72 h after ERCP). The conclusion is not yet uniform.

Objective

To systematically analyze the efficacy and safety of early LC and delayed LC in patients with gallstones and common bile duct stones after ERCP, to provide current high-level evidence-based medical evidence for clinical decision-making, to help clinicians optimize the diagnosis and treatment process, to reduce the occurrence of adverse complications caused by treatment.

Method

PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, Scopus, and other databases were searched to collect randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing early LC and delayed LC after ERCP from inception to December 2025. Two reviewers independently screened literature, extracted data, and assessed the risk of bias of included studies using the Cochrane ROB evaluation tool. The RevMan 5.4 software was used to analyze the outcomes of each group. Unlike previous meta-analyses, this study only included randomized controlled trials and incorporated the latest ones. Moreover, the quality of each outcome indicator was evaluated using the GRADE method.

Result

This meta-analysis included 7 randomized controlled trials involving 593 patients (296 in the early LC group and 297 in the delayed LC group). Compared with the delayed LC group, the early LC group was associated with a significantly lower rate of conversion to open surgery (RR = 0.35, 95% CI: 0.17-0.68, P = 0.002), shorter operation time (MD = -14.37 min, 95% CI: -28.22 to -0.51, P = 0.04), shorter postoperative hospital stay (MD = -0.81 days, 95% CI: -1.20 to -0.42, P < 0.0001), and lower incidence of incision infection (RR = 0.21, 95% CI: 0.07-0.61, P = 0.004). No significant difference was observed between the two groups in the incidence of bile leakage (RD = -0.04, 95% CI: -0.12-0.04, P = 0.30).

Conclusion

In conclusion, the available RCT evidence suggests that early LC following successful ERCP may provide clinical advantages over delayed LC, including lower conversion and infection rates and shorter operative and postoperative hospital stay. However, because of outcome-level heterogeneity, the limited number of included trials, and few bile-leakage events, these findings should be interpreted with caution and further verified in larger well-designed RCTs.

title: Free flap selection strategies and advances in facial soft tissue defect reconstruction.
abstract: Reconstruction of facial soft tissue defects remains a demanding task in plastic, reconstructive, and head and neck surgery because the face combines aesthetic units with essential functions such as oral competence, speech, swallowing, breathing, eyelid protection, and facial expression. The severity, depth, and composition of the defect are the primary determinants of flap selection, especially when defects extend beyond skin and subcutaneous tissue to expose the oral cavity, pharynx, nasal cavity, skull base, or critical structures. This narrative review summarizes evidence and technical progress regarding free flap selection for facial soft tissue reconstruction. Literature was identified through PubMed, Web of Science, and Google Scholar using combinations of the terms "facial soft tissue defect," "free flap," "perforator flap," and "virtual surgical planning." Priority was given to systematic reviews, meta-analyses, clinical series, and studies published between 2019 and 2026, while classic microsurgical reports were retained when foundational. Free flap choice should be guided by an integrative three-dimensional matrix: defect characteristics×patient profile×institutional resources. The anterolateral thigh flap remains a workhorse for moderate to large defects because of its thickness, long pedicle, availability of fascia lata, and nerve harvest. The radial forearm free flap remains valuable for thin and pliable resurfacing of the lips, eyelids, nasal lining, and oral lining. The deep inferior epigastric perforator flap is useful for large-volume contour restoration. Additional soft tissue options-including the lateral arm, parascapular, and medial sural artery perforator flaps-should be considered when color match, donor-site morbidity, or body habitus makes traditional workhorse flaps suboptimal. Facial soft tissue reconstruction requires not only flap survival but also restoration of contour, sensation, oral competence, facial animation, donor-site acceptability, and patient-reported quality of life. Mature technologies such as CTA, selective ultrasound, virtual surgical planning, intraoperative indocyanine green angiography, and structured postoperative monitoring should be distinguished from evolving tools such as augmented reality, artificial intelligence decision support, robotic-assisted anastomosis, artificial vascular conduits, and allogeneic or xenogeneic transplantation. Future research should focus on multicenter registries, standardized outcome measures, cost-effectiveness analyses, and externally validated decision-support models.

title: Clinical outcomes of one-hole split endoscope versus unilateral biportal endoscopy for lumbar degenerative diseases.
abstract: Objective This study aims to compare the clinical efficacy and safety of the novel One-hole Split Endoscope (OSE) technique with the established Unilateral Biportal Endoscopy (UBE) technique for the treatment of lumbar degenerative diseases (LDD). Methods A retrospective cohort study was conducted from January 2021 to December 2023, involving 116 patients with LDD. Patients were allocated to either the OSE group ( n = 60) or the UBE group ( n = 56). Perioperative outcomes (operative time, blood loss, hospital stay, incision length), clinical scores (VAS for back/leg pain, ODI), and complication rates were systematically compared between the two groups. Results Both groups demonstrated significant clinical improvement postoperatively. The OSE procedure required a longer operative time (135.8 ± 12.6 min vs. 102.4 ± 10.9 min, P < 0.001). However, the OSE group demonstrated advantages in several key perioperative metrics, including a significantly shorter hospital stay (3.9 ± 0.8 days vs. 5.4 ± 1.1 days, P < 0.001) and a smaller incision length (1.5 ± 0.2 cm vs. 2.7 ± 0.3 cm, P < 0.001). Intraoperative blood loss was minimal and comparable between the two groups ( P > 0.05). The OSE group also showed earlier and superior functional recovery, evidenced by significantly lower ODI scores at 1-week, 1-month, and final follow-up ( P < 0.05), whereas no significant differences were found in postoperative pain VAS scores or in the overall complication rate ( P = 0.127). Conclusion Both OSE and UBE techniques are effective and safe for treating LDD. Despite a longer operative time, the OSE technique offers distinct advantages in minimizing surgical trauma, promoting faster recovery, and achieving better early functional outcomes. OSE represents a valuable and innovative minimally invasive option in the spine surgeon's arsenal.

title: Preoperative staging of gastric cancer: a prospective comparison of gastric filling ultrasonography and enhanced CT with implications for surgical decision-making.
abstract: Background Accurate preoperative staging is essential for optimizing treatment strategies in gastric cancer. While gastric-enhanced CT is widely used, its accuracy remains suboptimal, particularly for early-stage tumors. Gastric filling ultrasonography, a non-invasive technique using oral contrast to displace intraluminal gas, offers potential advantages in mural visualization. This prospective study compared the diagnostic performance of gastric filling ultrasonography and gastric-enhanced CT against postoperative pathological staging. Methods We enrolled 406 patients with histologically confirmed gastric cancer who underwent both imaging modalities prior to surgery. Preoperative T and N stages assigned by each modality were compared with pathological results. Diagnostic accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and area under the ROC curve (AUC) were calculated. McNemar's test was used for paired comparisons, DeLong test for AUC comparisons, and Kappa statistics for agreement assessment. Univariate logistic regression identified factors affecting ultrasound accuracy. Results For T-staging, overall accuracy was 72.7% (295/406) for ultrasound vs. 63.5% (258/406) for CT ( P < 0.001). Ultrasound significantly outperformed CT in T1 (81.5% vs. 56.3%, P = 0.009) and T2 (81.1% vs. 67.9%, P < 0.001) stages. For N-staging, accuracy was 82.0% (333/406) for ultrasound vs. 60.1% (244/406) for CT ( P < 0.001). Kappa agreement with pathology was substantial for ultrasound T-staging ( κ = 0.625) and N-staging ( κ = 0.748), compared with moderate agreement for CT ( κ = 0.508 and 0.395, respectively). In multivariate analysis, vascular infiltration was the only independent factor associated with ultrasound T-staging accuracy. Conclusions Gastric filling ultrasonography demonstrates superior accuracy over gastric-enhanced CT for preoperative T1/T2 and N-staging, with substantial agreement with pathological findings. This non-invasive and radiation-free examination method can serve as an effective complement to CT, and is particularly suitable for gastric cancer at the T1 and T2 stages. We have proposed a complementary imaging protocol to assist in surgical decision-making, which is expected to enable clinicians to make more accurate preoperative staging assessments for patients with gastric cancer. Registration It was registered in the ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05596864).

title: Modern hysteroscopic management of congenital uterine anomalies: current techniques, emerging technologies, and future directions.
abstract: Background Congenital uterine anomalies are clinically relevant in reproductive medicine, particularly among women with infertility, recurrent pregnancy loss, adverse obstetric outcomes, or obstructive symptoms. Hysteroscopy has transformed the management of correctable intracavitary anomalies by enabling conservative, image-guided reconstruction of the uterine cavity while avoiding the morbidity of historical abdominal metroplasty. Scope This narrative review critically examines contemporary hysteroscopic management of septate uterus, dysmorphic uterus, bicorporeal septate uterus and rare obstructive malformations, such as Robert's uterus. We discuss the implications of the ESHRE/ESGE, CUME, and ASRM classification systems; the role of three-dimensional transvaginal ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging in preoperative mapping; and the technical principles that guide metroplasty, cavity remodeling, ultrasound-guided hysteroscopy, office-based metroplasty, and staged approaches in complex anatomy. Discussion Bipolar saline-based platforms, miniaturized resectoscopes, bipolar needle electrodes, cold scissors, and selected tissue removal systems have expanded the therapeutic spectrum and improved safety. The evidence supporting surgery remains heterogeneous: the TRUST randomized trial challenged routine septum resection in unselected women, whereas data for T-shaped and other dysmorphic uteri remain largely observational. Emerging technologies, including laser platforms, artificial intelligence-assisted hysteroscopy, and robotic concepts, are promising, but currently lack prospective validation. Conclusion Optimal management should therefore be individualized, anatomy-driven, and grounded in shared decision-making, with careful preservation of endometrium and myometrium. Standardized reporting, multicenter registries, and prospective comparative studies are needed to define which patients benefit most from hysteroscopic correction.

title: Case Report: Solitary fibrous tumor (SFT) of cerebellum: report of 2 cases.
abstract: Objective To elucidate the neuroradiological characteristics, clinical manifestations, and surgical outcomes of intracranial cerebellar solitary fibrous tumors (SFTs) to improve diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic strategies. Method A retrospective analysis was conducted on the clinical data of two histopathologically confirmed cases of cerebellar SFT, supplemented by a review of the relevant literature. Results Both patients underwent total surgical excision followed by postoperative radiotherapy. At the latest follow-up, neither patient showed radiological evidence of tumor recurrence (Case 1: 18 months; Case 2: 12 months]). Given the potential for late recurrence in SFTs, long-term surveillance is mandatory. Conclusion Intracranial cerebellar SFTs are rare neoplasms that are frequently misdiagnosed despite exhibiting distinctive magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) features. Definitive diagnosis relies on histopathological and immunohistochemical analyses. In this study, MRI demonstrated T1-weighted imaging (T1WI) hypointensity or isointensity, T2-weighted imaging (T2WI) heterogeneity, and inconsistent post-contrast enhancement. Immunohistochemical evaluation revealed positivity for CD34, CD99, and STAT6. Prompt surgical intervention accompanied by adjuvant therapy was associated with a favorable prognosis.

title: Pseudo-cerebrospinal fluid rhinorrhea following endoscopic endonasal transsphenoidal surgery for PitNET: a case report and literature review.
abstract: Pseudo-cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) rhinorrhea, defined as non-CSF nasal discharge mimicking true CSF leakage, is a rare but clinically significant complication that may prompt unnecessary aggressive treatment. We report a case of a 64-year-old man who developed positional clear nasal discharge after endoscopic endonasal resection of recurrent pituitary neuroendocrine tumor (PitNET). Glucose oxidase testing was negative, and imaging demonstrated intact skull base reconstruction. Nasal endoscopy revealed bilateral crusting and purulent secretions without evidence of CSF leak. The condition was diagnosed as vasomotor rhinitis. Conservative management-including nasal debridement, antibiotic therapy, topical corticosteroids, and saline irrigation-led to complete symptom resolution. This case underscores the importance of differentiating pseudo-CSF rhinorrhea from true CSF rhinorrhea to avoid invasive interventions.

title: Case Report: Solitary fibrous tumor of the right temporal skull base with bone destruction and postoperative recurrence.
abstract: Background Solitary fibrous tumor (SFT) is a rare fibroblastic mesenchymal neoplasm of the central nervous system, and temporal skull-base lesions with destructive osseous change and extension toward the middle-ear region are uncommon. Case presentation A 60-year-old woman presented with acute right peripheral facial weakness. CT demonstrated expansile mixed lytic-sclerotic destruction of the right temporal bone and middle cranial fossa floor, and MRI showed a 46 × 38 × 36 mm lobulated mass with heterogeneous signal, irregular peripheral and nodular enhancement, central nonenhancing necrotic or cystic change, and adjacent temporal-lobe edema. Right frontotemporal microsurgical resection achieved gross-total macroscopic removal, although piecemeal resection rendered microscopic margins unassessable. Histology and immunohistochemistry supported SFT, with 4 mitoses/10 high-power fields, focal necrosis, nuclear STAT6 expression, weak partial CD34 expression, MDM2 immunoreactivity, and a Ki-67 labeling index of approximately 40%. Review of the available sections showed no morphologically distinct high-grade sarcomatous component. Under the 2021 CNS WHO framework, the documented mitotic count corresponds most closely to grade 1. Postoperative radiotherapy was recommended but declined. Telephone follow-up indicated that outside-hospital MRI reportedly showed tumor recurrence at 18 months and further enlargement at 27 months. The patient also reported that outside examinations showed no metastatic disease in the lungs, liver, or skeleton. During later follow-up, the family expressed concern that the patient might not tolerate another major surgical intervention, and continued clinical and imaging follow-up was recommended. Conclusion This case illustrates that a documented mitotic count within the CNS WHO grade 1 range does not exclude clinically significant local recurrence. In skull-base SFT, formal pathologic grading should be interpreted together with anatomic extent, margin assessability, proliferative features, and the certainty of local control when planning postoperative management and surveillance.

title: Age is the wrong axis: rethinking surgical selection for octogenarians with early-stage non-small cell lung cancer.
abstract: Lung cancer is increasingly a disease of older age, and as low-dose computed tomography screening extends into the ninth decade, a growing number of octogenarians present with early-stage, potentially curable non-small cell lung cancer. Faced with these patients, clinicians repeatedly ask a single question: is this patient too old for surgery? Recent prospective data show that selected octogenarians achieve long-term survival comparable to younger patients despite substantially higher complication rates, with quality of life that recovers over the first postoperative year. Yet the favorable result is attributed to careful selection that is rarely defined, and is seldom accompanied by any account of the patients who were assessed and not offered an operation. This article argues that chronological age is the wrong axis for the decision. Physiologic reserve, measurable through validated frailty instruments and established physiologic testing, predicts postoperative outcome far better than birth year, and aging is sufficiently heterogeneous that any age threshold misclassifies patients in both directions. A substantial competing risk of non-cancer death, compounded by overdiagnosis among screen-detected tumors, tempers the survival gain expected from aggressive treatment and makes overtreatment as real a hazard as age-based exclusion. A graded menu of options now exists, extending from minimally invasive lobectomy through sublobar resection and stereotactic ablative radiotherapy to active surveillance, and intensity should descend with reserve rather than with age. The task is to operationalize careful selection through structured geriatric assessment, multidisciplinary collaboration, prehabilitation, and shared decision-making, and to judge success by outcomes that older patients actually value.

title: Case Report: Presumptive subdural hemorrhage as a rare neurological manifestation of primary immune-mediated thrombocytopenia in a dog.
abstract: A 10-year-old female spayed mixed-breed dog was presented with a history of seizures and acute progressive intracranial signs. The neurological examination was consistent with multifocal brain disease. Clinical examination revealed ecchymoses, petechiae, and bilateral retinal hemorrhage. Clinicopathological evaluation identified severe thrombocytopenia [a platelet count of 9 × 10 3 /μL without clumps on manual smear evaluation] with an increased mean platelet volume. Coagulation testing (activated partial thromboplastin time and prothrombin time) and fibrinolysis markers (D-dimers, quantitative fibrinogen), infectious disease screening, and thoracic and abdominal imaging were within normal limits, establishing a diagnosis of primary immune-mediated thrombocytopenia (ITP). Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain showed minimally expanded, bilateral crescent-shaped, extra-axial fluid accumulations overlying both cerebral hemispheres. Based on T1-weighted and T2-weighted hyperintensities and peripheral susceptibility artifact on T2*-weighted gradient-recalled echo (GRE) imaging, a late subacute subdural intracranial hemorrhage was diagnosed. Despite initial uneventful anesthesia and recovery, the dog experienced acute neurological deterioration and suffered cardiopulmonary arrest, suspected due to ongoing hemorrhage or brain herniation. This report describes a rare neurological manifestation of primary ITP in a dog. title: A European algorithm and strategy for management of chronic postoperative inguinal pain (EurA-CPIP).
abstract: Background Chronic postoperative inguinal pain (CPIP) is a disabling complication affecting 8%-17% of all patients after inguinal hernia repair. It is a complex pain condition with several pathophysiological mechanisms involved, including neuropathic pain, inflammation, and mechanical effects (e.g., mesh or scar tissue). Management remains inconsistent, probably due to limited high-quality evidence, heterogeneous approach, and insufficient standardisation of outcomes. This study aimed to develop EurA-CPIP, a multidisciplinary treatment algorithm and prospective data-collection platform designed to support consistent phenotyping, step-up management, and standardised outcomes across centres, creating an iterative platform for future hypothesis-driven research and multicentre trials. Methods An international multidisciplinary working group from European tertiary referral centres developed the European Algorithm and Strategy for Management of Chronic Postoperative Inguinal Pain (EurA-CPIP). Development was informed by the evidence synthesis underpinning the updated international HerniaSurge guidelines and a critical appraisal of previously published CPIP algorithms. A pragmatic step-up algorithm was designed, integrating pharmacological, interventional, surgical and supportive treatments, with prospective outcome registration and planned data-driven revision on a regular basis. Results EurA-CPIP provides a multidisciplinary algorithm with entry at multiple levels depending on prior treatment attempts. The concept is to begin and, if needed, advance from conservative measures such as systemic medication and topical therapy, to more invasive treatments such as trigger point injections, and ultrasound-guided nerve blocks; predefined investigational add-ons (radiofrequency, cryoneurolysis, botulinum toxin A) are embedded after documented block response. Multidisciplinary team review precedes escalation to more invasive interventions such as surgery. A supportive and rehabilitative coping trajectory is integrated early on. Standardised outcomes include patient-reported pain outcomes, functional impairment, psychological factors, analgesic use, and patient global impression of improvement. Conclusion EurA-CPIP is a pragmatic consensus-based strategy intended to harmonise and improve specialised CPIP care while utilising existing and developing emerging therapies. Future research should investigate pathophysiology and intervention effects within this step-up algorithm.

title: Extended Reality for Image-Guided Small Animal Surgery: Current Evidence, Clinical Applications, and Future Directions.
abstract: Image-guided surgery has become an integral component of modern veterinary surgery using advanced imaging modalities, such as computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging, ultrasonography, and fluoroscopy. Recently, extended reality (XR) technologies have emerged as promising tools to enhance image-guided surgical procedures by improving three-dimensional anatomical understanding, surgical navigation, and intraoperative decision-making. Although XR has gained considerable attention in human surgery, its application in veterinary surgery remains at an early stage. This narrative review aimed to provide a comprehensive overview of the current evidence regarding XR technologies in small animal surgery, with particular emphasis on their integration with preoperative and intraoperative imaging modalities. The available literature was reviewed to evaluate current clinical applications, technological developments and future perspectives. A literature search was performed in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science for studies published up to May 2026 using combinations of terms related to extended reality and small animal veterinary surgery. Original articles, case reports, pilot studies, technical reports, and reviews addressing clinical, experimental, or simulation-based applications were considered. Although several studies have explored the use of XR technologies for veterinary education, anatomical training, and diagnostic imaging instruction, relatively few investigations have assessed their direct application in clinical surgical practice. Potential applications have been described in orthopedic, oncologic, neurologic, cardiovascular, and minimally invasive procedures. Crucially, the currently available peer-reviewed evidence is restricted to canine patients, as no eligible feline studies were identified. Current evidence suggests that XR is an emerging technology with potential applications in canine surgical planning, image-guided procedures, and surgical training. Further prospective clinical studies are required to establish its clinical effectiveness, cost-effectiveness, and impact on surgical outcomes.

title: Rat Calvarial Defect Models in Bone Regeneration Research: A Narrative Review of Critical Size and Micro-Computed Tomography Outcome Reporting.
abstract: The rat calvarial defect model supports the preclinical evaluation of bone-regenerative approaches relevant to craniofacial reconstruction, including recombinant human bone morphogenetic protein-2 (rhBMP-2) and bone substitutes. However, its invasive nature requires study-specific harm-benefit assessment and application of the 3Rs. This narrative review used a structured PubMed search to examine spontaneous healing in defects smaller than 5 mm and μCT outcome reporting in untreated or control defects. Twenty-four studies of sub-5 mm defects and 45 μCT studies were included. Complete spontaneous healing was not reported in the sub-5 mm studies; only two μCT studies reported regeneration of at least 50% according to their respective outcome measures. Healing generally increased with longer observation periods and smaller defects, although methodological heterogeneity limited comparisons. Inconsistent reporting of acquisition parameters, segmentation thresholds, regions of interest, and numerical outcomes restricted reproducibility and data reuse. Within this PubMed-indexed evidence base, the findings support 5 mm defects as a practical model of incomplete spontaneous healing and indicate that smaller defects also do not reliably heal completely within the observation periods studied. These findings do not directly establish clinical benefit. Future studies should justify the least burdensome model capable of answering the research question, implement replacement, reduction, and refinement, and report standardized bone volume fractions, relevant measures of defect bridging, reproducible imaging methods, and reusable numerical data.

title: Gill Alterations in Adult Zebrafish Exposed to Avobenzone: Morphometric Profiling and Machine-Learning Analysis.
abstract: Gill histopathology is widely used in fish toxicology, but lesion scores and targeted measurements capture only part of the structural information in routine sections. We tested whether a morphometric profile could quantify avobenzone-related changes in adult zebrafish gills. The 40× dataset comprised gill sections from 35 adult zebrafish across five conditions represented in the image dataset: a 4-day solvent-control group and fish exposed to nominal avobenzone concentrations of 3 or 9 μg/L for 4 or 21 days. From 750 fields, quality control and automated segmentation yielded 503 accepted masks; 360 fields (72 per condition) were used in the balanced analysis. Thirty-nine descriptors quantified tissue geometry, interlamellar spaces, branch-like organisation, and thickness heterogeneity. Validation was repeated 30 times with all fields from each fish kept in the same partition. The time-matched 4-day control-versus-exposed comparison reached 89.4 ± 4.1% balanced accuracy. The 3-versus-9 μg/L comparison at 4 days reached 88.7 ± 4.6%, and 4 versus 21 days within the 9 μg/L group reached 88.5 ± 5.0%. Performance for direct five-condition classification was lower (68.4 ± 5.1%). Because 21-day control images were not included, exposure-related inference was restricted to the time-matched 4-day comparison. Morphometric profiling provides a quantitative complement to conventional histopathology while preserving individual fish identity as the grouping unit for image analysis.

title: Opportunistic Cardiovascular Assessment During Lung Cancer Screening with Low-Dose Computed Tomography: A New Window for Prevention.
abstract: Population-based lung cancer screening with low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) is expanding across Europe, including a publicly funded Polish programme starting in October 2026. Because screening-eligible individuals share substantial tobacco-related cardiovascular risk, LDCT also offers cardiovascular risk assessment without additional radiation. We conducted a narrative review of the PubMed literature published up to September 2026, prioritising guidelines, lung cancer screening cohorts and systematic reviews. We summarise the cardiovascular findings on non-contrast, non-electrocardiography (ECG)-gated LDCT: coronary artery, aortic valve, mitral annular and thoracic aortic calcification, ascending aortic dilatation, pericardial effusion, and pulmonary artery enlargement, as well as investigational cardiac volumetry, epicardial adipose tissue and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted quantification. We grade each finding by reportability, defined downstream action and supporting evidence, and align reporting thresholds with the European Respiratory Society/European Society of Thoracic Imaging (ERS/ESTI) statement on incidental findings. LDCT cannot replace dedicated cardiac imaging or establish haemodynamic diagnoses. The prognostic value of coronary and aortic valve calcification and of ascending aortic dilatation is established, whereas the evidence for mitral annular calcification and pulmonary artery enlargement is more limited; observational data indicate that reporting these markers changes preventive management, but whether this improves cardiovascular outcomes has not yet been demonstrated. Standardised reporting, proportionate thresholds, and coordinated pathways linking radiology, pulmonology, primary care and cardiology are needed to translate incidental cardiovascular findings into scalable prevention and should be evaluated in implementation studies.

title: Spectral-Distribution Uncertainty Modeling for Robust Cross-Domain Medical Image Segmentation.
abstract: Domain generalization (DG) for medical image segmentation is commonly approached by simulating domain shifts through deterministic image transformations or feature perturbations. However, such methods implicitly assume that unseen domains can be approximated by predefined appearance variations. In this work, we challenge this assumption and hypothesize that medical domain shifts are more fundamentally characterized as uncertainty in spectral distributions. While anatomical structures are largely preserved across institutions, scanners, and acquisition protocols, substantial variations arise in image appearance, texture, and artifacts, which are predominantly manifested in the spectral domain. To test this hypothesis, we propose Spectral-Distribution Uncertainty (SDU), a frequency-aware DG framework that explicitly models uncertainty in the Fourier amplitude distributions of intermediate representations. By decomposing Transformer features into amplitude and phase components, SDU disentangles domain-specific spectral characteristics from domain-invariant anatomical semantics. Instead of imposing handcrafted frequency perturbations, SDU estimates spectral-distribution uncertainty during training and injects stochastic variations into the amplitude space, synthesizing diverse yet anatomically consistent representations that emulate potential unseen domains. Consequently, SDU expands the support of spectral feature distributions, enabling the model to learn representations that are robust to uncertainty-induced spectral shifts. Extensive experiments on retinal fundus and prostate MRI benchmarks demonstrate that SDU consistently outperforms state-of-the-art DG methods. Beyond empirical gains, these findings provide evidence that medical domain shifts are more appropriately characterized as uncertainty in spectral feature distributions, offering a principled perspective for generalizable medical image segmentation.

title: VesselRegNet: Multi-Scale Feature Fusion Network for Multi-Modal Joint Retinal Vessel Segmentation and Registration.
abstract: Multimodal retinal image registration remains challenging due to nonlinear intensity discrepancies and insufficient feature representation across modalities. To address these limitations, we propose VesselRegNet, a joint retinal vessel segmentation and registration framework based on multi-scale feature fusion. The model integrates a multi-scale semantic feature extraction module with a shared prediction head and rotation-equivariant constraints to enhance feature consistency. Unlike conventional approaches relying on binary segmentation masks, the proposed method utilizes dense semantic features to directly guide deformable registration. Experimental results demonstrate that VesselRegNet achieves an average Dice coefficient of 0.664 and SSIM of 0.645, achieving a relative improvement of 4.1% in Dice and 2.5% in SSIM over the strongest baseline (RetinaRegNet), and up to 11.9% improvement over general unsupervised registration frameworks. The proposed multi-scale fusion and joint learning strategy improves registration accuracy under complex retinal deformations.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Selective Prediction in Brain-Tumour MRI Classification: Selective Risk Reduction and Component-Wise Reliability Findings.
abstract: Background Automated brain-MRI analysis is usually judged by accuracy at a single operating point, yet a model that is accurate on average may still fail without signalling that it is about to fail. Selective prediction addresses this by allowing a model to abstain, but the resulting trade-off between coverage and risk is rarely quantified in medical imaging. Objective This study asks whether confidence- and entropy-based selective prediction produces a measurable reduction in selective risk in a biomedical vision-language classifier by concentrating errors among withheld cases, and at what coverage cost. Three further components of a brain-MRI-analysis framework-volumetric segmentation, glioma grading and structured report generation-are evaluated as complementary evidence about the reliability profiles of different modules, not as independent contributions. Methods A LoRA-fine-tuned LLaVA-Med classifier was evaluated on the 1000-image BRISC2025 test partition, with a disjunctive rejection rule based on softmax confidence and predictive entropy. Volumetric segmentation used nnU-Net v2 (3D full-resolution) on BraTS2020 with a three-fold ensemble evaluated on 74 held-out cases; glioma grading (high- versus low-grade) used DenseNet121 on multi-slice representations; report generation used Meta Llama 3.2 3B Instruct fine-tuned with QLoRA on structured findings. All proportions are reported with 95% Wilson score intervals under a single analysis plan documented before the reported analyses were finalised. Results Withholding 1.80% of predictions (95% CI 1.14-2.83) raised selective accuracy to 97.76% (95% CI 96.63-98.52) and reduced selective risk from 3.40% to 2.24%, a relative reduction of 34.1%. Withheld predictions were strongly enriched for errors (66.7% versus 2.24%; odds ratio 87.3, Fisher exact p = 4.6 × 10 -15 ), capturing 35.3% of all errors while issuing 99.38% of the predictions that were correct. Considered as a detector of its own errors, the rule has a balanced accuracy of 67.34%; this describes the binary rejection decision at the realised threshold and does not identify the AUROC of the underlying continuous score, which the single operating point leaves anywhere in [0.351, 0.996]. Because the per-sample probability vectors were not retained, the full risk-coverage curve, the rule ablations and calibration error could not be computed, and the thresholds (τ c = 0.6, τ H = 1.0) were selected empirically on an undocumented partition; the selective-prediction finding is therefore reported as a single-operating-point case study and is exploratory. Among the complementary components, three-fold ensembling improved held-out mean Dice from 0.7948 to 0.8150 (+0.0202), reported descriptively because the per-case values needed for a paired test were not preserved. Glioma grading did not achieve better-than-chance discrimination: balanced accuracy 49.91%, Cohen's κ -0.0023, Matthews correlation coefficient -0.0026, low-grade recall 8.96% (95% CI 5.81-13.57), and accuracy (74.03%) below a constant majority-class classifier (79.46%); the associated McNemar statistic is reported descriptively because slice-level observations are not independent. Report generation produced high automatic similarity scores (BERTScore F1 0.9513) that are not interpretable without baselines. Conclusions Confidence- and entropy-based abstention produced a measurable reduction in selective risk at low rejection rates, and it did so because errors concentrated among the cases were withheld by the confidence/entropy rule rather than because predictions were discarded indiscriminately. At the realised coverage the rule captured 65.5% (95% bootstrap CI 41.9-87.8) of the reduction achievable by an oracle that rejects only true errors. The component-wise comparison shows that this reliability behaviour cannot be assumed for every module: high aggregate accuracy and useful discrimination came apart in the grading task. These findings are component-wise and do not constitute an end-to-end, externally validated or clinically validated pipeline. The vision-language evaluation is at image level: BRISC2025 carries no patient identifiers, so patient-level independence cannot be established and the reported intervals should be read with that constraint in mind.

The component-wise comparison shows that this reliability behaviour cannot be assumed for every module: high aggregate accuracy and useful discrimination came apart in the grading task. These findings are component-wise and do not constitute an end-to-end, externally validated or clinically validated pipeline. The vision-language evaluation is at image level: BRISC2025 carries no patient identifiers, so patient-level independence cannot be established and the reported intervals should be read with that constraint in mind.

title: DU-KAN: A Dual-Domain Enhanced Deep-Learning Framework for Digital Pathology-Based Oxford MEST-C Assessment in Pediatric IgA Nephropathy.
abstract: Oxford MEST-C assessment of pediatric immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN) relies on pathologists' interpretation of complex renal biopsy structures. Automated segmentation may support standardized quantification but is challenged by scale variation, weak boundaries, and small lesions. We developed DU-KAN, a stage-adapted U-KAN framework combining a shallow convolution-MaxViT dual-branch encoder with adapted heterogeneous feature fusion and wavelet-prototype skip enhancement. A single-center dataset of 532 periodic acid-Schiff-stained images from 278 children was partitioned at the patient level. On the held-out test set of 55 patients, DU-KAN achieved a mean Dice of 69.58% across eight classes, including background (95% patient-level bootstrap CI, 66.23-71.91), exceeding U-KAN by 3.56 percentage points (95% CI, 1.90-5.26). Foreground mean Dice was 65.42%. On the Synapse abdominal CT benchmark, mean Dice across eight organs was 87.21%, supporting cross-task architectural generalization, rather than external validation in pediatric IgAN. Segmentation outputs were further aggregated into case-level MEST-C-related indicators. In an exploratory 40-case evaluation, complete agreement across the five assessed indicators was 65.00% (26/40), while sensitivity was 37.50% for E (3/8) and 50.00% for T (1/2). The 97.50% agreement for T largely reflected the predominance of negative cases and did not establish reliable positive-case detection. DU-KAN improves the internal segmentation performance and achieves structured pathological quantification, which can provide auxiliary reference for clinical judgment of renal pathologists.

title: VLM-Based Mesh Segmentation Framework for DDH Robotic Ultrasound.
abstract: For robotic ultrasound targeting developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH), reconstructed infant body-surface meshes should preserve the target surface while excluding bed, support, and background geometry. This study proposes a structured vision-language model (VLM)-based multi-view segmentation method for infant phantom mesh cleanup. Text-guided 2D masks provide foreground and background evidence; mask-quality statistics and structured VLM assessments generate view-specific foreground-support weights that undergo deterministic risk suppression before target/non-target classification of 3D vertices. Hard voting and Rule-weighted voting were baselines under identical projection and post-processing settings. We evaluated one physical infant phantom across 150 separate acquisition-reconstruction trials under controlled conditions, each comprising 40 voting views and 10 held-out evaluation views, yielding 1500 manually annotated reference masks. Structured VLM voting achieved a Balanced score (intersection over union minus the 2-pixel tolerant leakage rate) of 0.804 ± 0.085, versus 0.801 ± 0.084 and 0.793 ± 0.086 for Rule-weighted and Hard voting. This leakage rate was 0.087 ± 0.043, versus 0.089 ± 0.042 and 0.092 ± 0.043; mean Coverage remained similar (0.992-0.993). The Balanced-score gain and leakage-rate reduction relative to Rule-weighted voting remained significant after Holm correction (adjusted p = 0.029 and p = 0.033, respectively). Validation using real-infant data, 3D reference standards, and closed-loop robotic scanning is still required.
