title: Lymphatic Microvascular Density, Lymphatic Invasion and Endothelial Cell Proliferation as Prognostic Biomarkers in Cutaneous Melanoma: A Systematic Review and Evidence Map.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Cutaneous melanoma spreads preferentially through the lymphatic system, and sentinel lymph node status is among the strongest prognostic factors. Whether tumour angiogenesis and lymphangiogenesis add prognostic information beyond conventional histopathology has been examined in many immunohistochemical studies, with heterogeneous results. We conducted a systematic review, reported according to PRISMA 2020 and not registered, of blood microvascular density (MVD), lymphatic vessel density (LVD) in the intratumoral and peritumoral compartments, proliferating (Ki-67-positive) lymphatic vessels and lymphatic invasion (LI) as prognostic markers in primary cutaneous melanoma. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE was searched to 10 September 2026, supplemented by a Web of Science export and by citation tracking of the reference meta-analysis by Pastushenko et al. (2014). Twenty-one cutaneous study units (25 reports) and four ocular studies providing indirect evidence were included, and risk of bias was rated with the QUIPS tool. Results: In the reference meta-analysis, peritumoral LVD and LI, but not MVD or intratumoral LVD, were associated with metastasis. The newer cohorts confirmed this pattern and provided adjusted effect sizes: peritumoral LVD predicted disease-free (HR 2.14) and melanoma-specific survival (HR of 2.74; 95% CI 1.31 to 5.73), immunohistochemically detected LI predicted sentinel node metastasis (33% vs. 11% positive nodes) and overall survival, and a Ki-67-positive lymphatic endothelium predicted melanoma-specific mortality (adjusted HR of 2.03; 95% CI 1.33 to 3.10) in 264 patients. Blood MVD and blood endothelial proliferation were not prognostic. Heterogeneity of markers, counting methods and effect measures precluded re-pooling. Conclusions: Peritumoral LVD, LI and proliferating lymphatics are promising adjunct biomarkers for selecting patients for sentinel node biopsy, adjuvant therapy and closer follow-up, pending standardised, digital-pathology-based quantification.

title: Clinical Utility of 18F-FDG PET/CT for Staging and Restaging of Pediatric Malignant Melanoma: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Malignant melanoma is a rare entity in the pediatric population, accounting for approximately 1-3% of all childhood malignancies. Despite its rarity, it is the most common skin cancer in children. Accurate staging and monitoring are essential for treatment planning and prognosis. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical value of 18F-FDG PET/CT in staging and restaging of pediatric malignant melanoma. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed pediatric patients aged 18 years or younger who underwent 18F-FDG PET/CT imaging between 2010 and 2025 with histopathologically confirmed malignant melanoma. Demographic data, primary lesion localization, PET/CT findings, pathology reports, and clinical outcomes were recorded. Lesions were categorized as positive and negative in the final analysis. Diagnostic performance parameters (with 95% confidence intervals (CIs)) were calculated using histopathological confirmation or clinical follow-up as the reference standard, and categorical associations were assessed using Fisher's exact test. Results: A total of 20 patients (12 females, 8 males; mean age: 11 years, range: 4-18) and 31 PET/CT examinations were included, with a mean follow-up duration of approximately 98 months. PET/CT was performed for initial staging in 17 examinations and for restaging in 14. On an examination-based analysis, PET/CT findings were negative in 22/31 (71.0%) and positive in 9/31 (29.0%) examinations. On a patient-based analysis, 12/20 (60%) patients had all examinations classified as true negative and remained disease-free throughout follow-up. 18F-FDG PET/CT demonstrated a sensitivity of 80.0% (95% CI: 49.0-94.3%), specificity of 95.2% (95% CI: 77.3-99.2%), positive predictive value of 88.9% (95% CI: 56.5-98.0%), negative predictive value of 90.9% (95% CI: 72.2-97.5%), and overall accuracy of 90.3% (95% CI: 75.1-96.7%) for the detection of clinically active disease. Agreement between PET/CT findings and clinical outcomes was substantial (Cohen's κ = 0.77). Among the nine PET-negative restaging examinations, one was subsequently confirmed as false-negative; the remaining eight showed no evidence of active disease during the available follow-up period. Conclusions: In this exploratory retrospective study, 18F-FDG PET/CT demonstrated promising diagnostic performance for staging and restaging of pediatric malignant melanoma, with high specificity and negative predictive value. These findings should be interpreted with caution given the small sample size and retrospective design but suggest a potentially meaningful role for 18F-FDG PET/CT in the multidisciplinary management of this rare pediatric malignancy.

title: Gut Failure During Pediatric Critical Illness: Toward a Phenotype-Driven Framework for Early Recognition, Prognostication, and Prevention.
abstract: Gastrointestinal dysfunction is common during critical illness, yet gut failure remains poorly defined, inconsistently diagnosed, and incompletely integrated into organ dysfunction frameworks. Current clinical approaches often recognize gut failure only after overt manifestations such as feeding intolerance, ileus, abdominal distension, gastrointestinal bleeding, or radiographic bowel injury have developed. However, these signs may represent late manifestations of distinct and potentially evolving pathophysiologic pathways. In this narrative review, we propose a phenotype-driven framework for gut failure during critical illness, with emphasis on pediatric critical care. We conceptualize gut failure as a dynamic syndrome comprising overlapping phenotypes: motility-dominant dysfunction, perfusion-ischemic injury, epithelial barrier failure, dysbiosis, absorptive-nutritional failure, treatment-modified dysfunction, and mixed evolving states. Linking these phenotypes to clinical presentation, prognosis, and management may improve early diagnosis and allow clinicians to anticipate progression before irreversible injury occurs. Pediatric patients represent a particularly vulnerable population because gut failure may affect not only short-term outcomes such as infection, mechanical ventilation, and mortality, but also nutrition delivery, growth, microbiome development, and recovery. A phenotype-based approach may shift gut failure from a late symptom-based diagnosis toward an earlier, mechanism-informed, and potentially preventable process.

title: MRI-Based Radiomics Model for Pretreatment Prediction of Pathological Lymph Node Metastasis in Neuroendocrine Carcinoma of the Cervix: Dual-Center Development and External Validation.
abstract: Objectives: To develop and externally validate MRI-based radiomics and clinicoradiomics models for predicting pathological lymph node metastasis (LNM) in neuroendocrine carcinoma of the cervix (NECC). Methods: This retrospective two-center study included 133 patients who underwent pretreatment pelvic MRI and pathological nodal assessment: 93 for development and 40 for external validation. Intratumoral and peritumoral features were extracted from T2-weighted, diffusion-weighted, and contrast-enhanced T1-weighted images. Stratified nested fivefold cross-validation evaluated the complete revised selection process. Locked models were assessed for discrimination, calibration, and exploratory net benefit, with conventional MRI nodal assessment as a comparator. Results: Pathological LNM was present in 54/133 patients (40.6%). The selected radiomics-only k-nearest neighbors (KNN) model had an external AUC of 0.783 (95% CI, 0.630 to 0.935), accuracy of 0.800, sensitivity of 0.813, and specificity of 0.792. The complete selection procedure yielded an out-of-fold AUC of 0.731. External AUCs were 0.727 for the clinical/MRI model and 0.767 for the clinicoradiomics model; neither fusion model differed significantly from the clinical/MRI comparator. Conventional MRI sensitivity was 0.563, with no significant paired difference from the selected model ( p = 0.125). External calibration was imperfect (Brier score, 0.186; slope, 0.672). Conclusions: MRI radiomics showed moderate external discrimination of pathological LNM in NECC. Adding clinical variables did not demonstrate further benefit. Multicenter validation, recalibration, and clinical-impact assessment are needed before clinical application.

title: CSFINet-Based Multimodal MRI Image Segmentation and Survival Prediction.
abstract: Background : Brain tumors are highly lethal malignant neoplasms, for which accurate tumor segmentation and survival-day prediction are critical to treatment planning and prognostic assessment. This study establishes an exploratory two-stage analytical framework spanning multimodal MRI tumor segmentation and survival-day prediction. Methods : The study is based on the BraTS 2020 multimodal MRI dataset, employing four imaging modalities-T1, T1ce, T2, and FLAIR-with patient age and extent-of-resection status as candidate clinical features. The 235 cases with survival labels were split at the patient level (188 training, 47 test; single 80:20 split). In the first stage, CSFINet is used for brain tumor segmentation; in the second stage, the resulting binary whole-tumor mask, age, and resection status serve as inputs for survival-day prediction. The survival models are trained on the ground-truth whole-tumor masks but evaluated on the masks predicted by CSFINet, and the survival training runs were not seeded. Four models-image-only, image with age, image with resection status, and image with both-are constructed for ablation experiments, and Gradient SHAP is introduced for interpretability analysis. Results : CSFINet achieves a Mean Dice, Mean Precision, and Mean Recall of 0.7849±0.1937, 0.8739±0.1978, and 0.7480±0.1936, compared with 0.5084, 0.8676, and 0.3822 for a U-Net baseline trained in this study under an identical configuration. The gains are in Dice and recall; the precision difference (+0.0063, 95% CI -0.0601 to 0.1086) is not distinguishable from zero. This comparison is internal to the present study; published BraTS 2020 results were obtained under different evaluation protocols and are not directly comparable. title: Preoperative White Matter Disease Severity Predicts Intraoperative Cerebral Desaturation During Carotid Endarterectomy.
abstract: Objective : Carotid endarterectomy carries the risk of cerebral ischemia during carotid clamping. Traditional risk stratification relies on anatomic factors such as contralateral stenosis, yet these predictors demonstrate limited sensitivity for intraoperative hypoperfusion. White matter hyperintensities (WMH), quantified by the Fazekas scale, reflect chronic cerebral small vessel disease and impaired cerebrovascular reactivity. Whether baseline WMH burden predicts intraoperative cerebral oxygen desaturation during carotid clamping remains unknown. Methods : This prospective, single-center cohort study enrolled patients undergoing carotid endarterectomy with continuous bilateral near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) monitoring. The primary outcome was the maximum contralateral regional cerebral oxygen saturation (rSO 2 ) decrease within 2 min after carotid clamp placement compared with the pre-clamp baseline. The primary predictor was the contralateral hemisphere Fazekas score assessed on preoperative brain MRI. Multivariable linear regression adjusted for age, contralateral carotid stenosis, clamping time, and shunt use. Results : Of 173 patients screened, 58 with complete data were included in the final analysis. Th average age was 69. 2 ± 7 years, 37.9% were female, significant contralateral stenosis was present in four cases, and the average exclusion time was 30.1 ± 9.7 min. In multivariable regression, a higher contralateral Fazekas score was independently associated with greater contralateral rSO 2 desaturation during carotid clamping (unstandardized β = 0.008, standardized β = 0.287, p = 0.035). The association remained statistically significant after adjustment for all covariates. The overall model explained 8.8% of variance in contralateral desaturation (R 2 = 0.088). Conclusions : Contralateral white matter disease severity, quantified by Fazekas score, was independently associated with greater contralateral cerebral oxygen desaturation during carotid clamping. This finding supports the concept that baseline microvascular disease modifies acute ischemic tolerance independent of large-vessel anatomy. Preoperative Fazekas scoring may enhance risk stratification and inform individualized neuromonitoring strategies during carotid endarterectomy.

title: Skene's Gland Malignancy from Imaging Diagnosis to Management: A Narrative Review.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Skene's gland malignancies are extremely rare tumors of the female paraurethral region, known almost exclusively from case reports and small case series. Their diagnosis is often delayed because symptoms are nonspecific and may mimic benign periurethral disorders, urethral diverticula, primary urethral carcinoma or anterior vaginal wall tumors. This narrative review focuses on the role of imaging, particularly pelvic magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), in the diagnosis, differential diagnosis, staging and treatment planning of Skene's gland malignancies, distinguishing evidence from confirmed Skene's gland cases from evidence extrapolated from female urethral carcinoma. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and Web of Science were searched on 27 September 2026 (publication years 2015-2026) and supplemented by reference-list screening; an explicit case definition was applied. Results: Of 191 records (93 after de-duplication), 17 reports of Skene's gland malignancy were included (15 case reports or series and 2 systematic reviews); fewer than thirty cases have been published overall. Patients were mostly postmenopausal (median age about 70 years, range 45-91), presenting with an asymptomatic periurethral nodule, hematuria or vaginal bleeding, or lower urinary tract symptoms; no uniform staging system has been applied. Most tumors were prostatic-type adenocarcinomas treated by local excision alone; radiotherapy, chemotherapy or androgen deprivation were used mainly for nodal, metastatic or recurrent disease. After examination, ultrasonography can detect and characterize a paraurethral mass, whereas MRI best defines tumor epicenter, urethral, periurethral and anterior vaginal wall involvement and regional spread, and should precede cystourethroscopy and biopsy; CT and PET/CT are complementary for systemic staging. No single immunohistochemical marker establishes Skene's gland origin. Conclusions: MRI is central to localizing and staging suspected Skene's gland malignancy and thus to guiding biopsy and the choice between local excision and radical surgery, but most imaging recommendations are extrapolated from female urethral carcinoma and require validation in pooled multicenter data.

title: Development and Patient-Level Internal Validation of an MRI-Based Radiomics Machine Learning Model for Preoperative Prediction of Cervical Lymph Node Metastasis in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Pilot Study.
abstract: Background / Objectives : Cervical lymph node metastasis (LNM) is the main prognostic factor in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) and guides the extent of neck treatment. This retrospective pilot study aimed to develop MRI-based radiomics machine learning models for the preoperative prediction of LNM in OSCC and to validate them internally at the patient level. Methods : Preoperative MRI of 74 patients (32 LNM-positive, 42 LNM-negative on histopathology) was analysed. In each patient the largest morphologically suspicious cervical lymph node was segmented volumetrically on axial contrast-enhanced T1-weighted images, and 1409 IBSI-compliant radiomic features were extracted. Performance was estimated by 10 repeats of 5-fold nested cross-validation with the patient as the unit of partitioning; standardisation, correlation pruning, LASSO selection, hyperparameter tuning and threshold choice were confined to the training folds. Six classifiers were compared. Results : LASSO retained a median of nine features (range 6-13). SVM performed best, with an AUC of 0.781 (95% CI 0.667-0.884), a sensitivity of 0.72, a specificity of 0.76 and a balanced accuracy of 0.74; XGBoost (AUC 0.774) and logistic regression (AUC 0.769) performed comparably. A slice-level analysis of the same data, in which slices from the same patient could fall into both training and test sets, gave an apparent AUC of 0.878 but a specificity of only 0.33. Conclusions : MRI radiomic features of cervical lymph nodes carry moderate patient-level information on LNM in OSCC, and slice-level designs can substantially misrepresent performance. External validation in larger multicentre cohorts is required before clinical use.

title: Metachronous Metastatic Invasive Breast Carcinoma and Metastatic Small Cell Carcinoma Clinically and Radiologically Favoured to Be of Pulmonary Origin: A Case Report.
abstract: Background: In patients with metastatic breast carcinoma, newly identified visceral or pulmonary lesions may represent progression of the known malignancy or, less commonly, a distinct second primary tumor. Histopathological and immunohistochemical evaluation is therefore essential for establishing tumor lineage and guiding treatment. Case Presentation: We report the case of a 46-year-old woman diagnosed in 2021 with metastatic hormone receptor-positive/HER2-negative breast carcinoma, presenting with a left breast mass and multiple osteolytic bone metastases. Histopathological examination demonstrated invasive breast carcinoma of no special type, with 98% estrogen receptor expression, 98% progesterone receptor expression, a Ki-67 proliferation index of 15%, and negative HER2 status. She received palliative radiotherapy for painful bone metastases and systemic treatment with letrozole and ribociclib. Five years later, she was evaluated for newly detected liver lesions. Positron emission tomography-computed tomography also demonstrated a metabolically active right centrohilar pulmonary lesion, although a primary lung tumor could not be definitively distinguished radiologically from nodal disease. Liver biopsy revealed a high-grade small-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma with positivity for TTF-1, chromogranin, synaptophysin, and CD56, a Ki-67 proliferation index of 85%, and negative GATA3 expression. These findings, together with the clinical and radiological features, favored a pulmonary origin. The patient was subsequently treated with cisplatin, etoposide, and atezolizumab. Discussion: This case illustrates the difficulty of distinguishing progression of metastatic breast carcinoma from a metachronous second malignancy. The markedly different morphology with a discordant neuroendocrine immunophenotypic profile together with the radiological and serological findings, favored a distinct second malignancy rather than progression of the known breast carcinoma. Conclusions: New metastatic-appearing lesions in patients with a known malignancy should not automatically be attributed to progression of the original cancer. Re-biopsy and integrated histopathological, immunohistochemical, clinical, and radiological assessment may identify a distinct second malignancy and substantially alter systemic treatment and clinical management.

title: Quantitative 0.55 T MRI of the Infraclavicular Brachial Plexus: Topography and Neurovascular Morphometry Relevant to Infraclavicular Block.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Quantitative MRI data describing the infraclavicular brachial plexus cords together with both axillary vessels remain limited. This study characterized artery-centered cord topography and neurovascular morphometry on 0.55 T MRI and discussed the potential anatomical implications for infraclavicular block. Methods: This prospective cross-sectional imaging study included 100 adults undergoing clinically indicated MRI. One infraclavicular region was analyzed per participant. Within the mid-infraclavicular retropectoral region posterior to the pectoralis minor muscle, the axial T1-weighted image providing the clearest simultaneous visualization of the lateral cord (LC), medial cord (MC), posterior cord (PC), axillary artery (AA), and axillary vein (AV) was selected. The LC, MC, PC, and AV were mapped using a 12-sector clock-face model centered on the AA, and center-to-center intercord, cord-to-AA, and cord-to-AV distances were measured. Results: The LC was most frequently located at 11 o'clock (62%), the MC at 3 o'clock (41%), the PC at 6 o'clock (40%), and the AV at 2 o'clock (71.1%; n = 90). Mean intercord distances were 11.73 ± 3.17 mm (LC-MC), 11.09 ± 2.43 mm (LC-PC), and 8.13 ± 2.83 mm (MC-PC). Mean cord-to-AA distances were 6.33 ± 1.69, 7.36 ± 2.03, and 7.13 ± 1.83 mm for LC, MC, and PC, respectively. In 92 participants with complete cord-to-AV measurements, corresponding means were 17.01 ± 5.01, 9.61 ± 2.90, and 16.54 ± 3.87 mm. Conclusions: At the mid-infraclavicular retropectoral level, 0.55 T MRI demonstrated a structured but non-equidistant neurovascular arrangement. These imaging-derived data provide quantitative anatomical reference information but are not procedural safety margins or predictors of block success.

title: Automated CMR Quantification of Pulmonary Artery Size-Based and Slow-Flow Metrics in Pulmonary Hypertension.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Pulmonary artery (PA) dilatation and slow-flow are imaging features of pulmonary hypertension (PH), but their quantitative assessment on routine cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) remains limited. This study aimed to develop and evaluate an automated CMR pipeline for quantifying PA size-based and slow-flow metrics from routine white-blood (WB) and black-blood (BB) acquisitions. Methods: A total of 205 CMR acquisitions (106 WB and 99 BB) were used for model development and independent testing. Separate deep learning nnU-Net-based segmentation models were developed for WB and BB acquisitions using a two-stage cascaded framework. Automated measurements included PA volume and PA slow-flow. The trained models were subsequently applied to a larger cohort of 1471 patients using available WB and BB acquisitions to assess automated measurement extraction and agreement with clinical reports. Results: Automated PA volumetric measurements demonstrated excellent agreement with manual reference measurements for both the WB and BB models (ICC 0.94 and 0.93, respectively), with high segmentation accuracy (Dice 0.86 and 0.80, respectively). Automated slow-flow measurements also demonstrated excellent volumetric agreement (ICC 0.94), despite lower spatial overlap (Dice 0.61). Automated slow-flow classification demonstrated 83% agreement with qualitative clinical reporting (κ = 0.58). Conclusions: Automated PA volumetric quantification from routine CMR is feasible. Automated slow-flow quantification showed promising performance but requires validation across scanner vendors and BB acquisition protocols before broader clinical application.

title: Calibration-Aware Patient-Level Prediction of Source-Defined MSIMUT Status in Colorectal Cancer from Whole-Slide Histopathology Images Using Foundation-Model Embeddings.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Microsatellite instability (MSI) is clinically important in colorectal cancer, but definitive assessment requires molecular or immunohistochemical testing. This study developed a leakage-safe, calibration-aware patient-level framework for predicting a source-defined MSIMUT category from hematoxylin-and-eosin whole-slide-derived patches using fixed Phikon foundation-model embeddings. Methods: The TCGA-derived colorectal cohort comprised 360 patients, including 65 source-defined positive and 295 MSS cases, represented by 192,312 pre-extracted patches. Patch embeddings were aggregated using mean, max, and mean-plus-max pooling, and downstream classifiers were evaluated under patient-level cross-validation with calibration, threshold, decision-curve, clinicopathological, source-provenance, and patch-count sensitivity analyses. Results: In the primary random patient-level evaluation, logistic regression with mean-plus-max pooling achieved a mean ROC-AUC of 0.915 and PR-AUC of 0.809. Fully nested Platt calibration yielded pooled out-of-sample ROC-AUC 0.913, PR-AUC 0.796, Brier score 0.073, calibration slope 1.037, and calibration-in-the-large 0.023. Within the internally cross-validated mean-plus-max framework, an exploratory sensitivity ≥ 0.95 operating point yielded sensitivity 0.969, specificity 0.393, and negative predictive value 0.983. Provenance reconstruction identified source-partition-dependent patch-count structure. Conclusions: These findings support the methodological feasibility of fixed foundation-model embeddings for internal MSI-related pre-screening research, while showing that apparent performance is sensitive to source structure. title: Photon-Counting Computed Tomography Enables Image-Guided Navigation of the Paranasal Sinuses at Ultra-Low Radiation Dose: An Initial Cadaveric Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives : Photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT) enables substantial radiation dose reduction while preserving high spatial resolution. Its potential for image-guided navigation in endoscopic sinus surgery (ESS), particularly at ultra-low dose levels, remains insufficiently explored. This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility of PCCT for four different surgical navigation systems at progressively reduced radiation doses. Methods : PCCT datasets of the paranasal sinuses were acquired from two cadaveric specimens using a standard protocol followed by stepwise dose reductions down to 5% of the reference dose. The datasets were used for image-guided navigation with four systems (one optical, three electromagnetic). Registration success, navigation accuracy, and user satisfaction (visual analog scale) were assessed at 100% and 5% dose levels using linear mixed-effects models. Results : Registration was successful for all navigation systems at every dose level. Mean navigation accuracy remained stable despite dose reduction (2.22 ± 1.16 mm at 100% vs. 1.93 ± 1.05 mm at 5% radiation dose; p = 0.364). User satisfaction regarding navigation was consistently high (mean 8.8 ± 0.75) and showed no significant differences between dose levels. Conclusions : PCCT enabled image-guided navigation even at ultra-low radiation doses down to 5% of standard exposure, without compromising navigation accuracy in this initial study. These findings highlight the potential of PCCT to substantially reduce radiation burden while maintaining clinical performance. Further in-human studies are needed.

title: Automated Segmentation of Mass Lesions in Mammography: Mask R-CNN Versus Classical Methods, Fuzzy Clustering and MedSAM.
abstract: Background/Objectives: The automatic and accurate segmentation of mass lesions in mammograms is a critical step in the computer-aided diagnosis workflow. This study evaluates the mask region-based convolutional neural network (Mask R-CNN), a robust deep learning model for instance-level segmentation, highlighting its growing potential in medical imaging. Methods: Following configuration optimization, the model is applied to mammography images from the CSAW-CC and TOMPEI-CMMDs, which provide masks annotated by breast radiology experts, to be used as a ground truth. To quantify shape and contour discrepancies with respect to the radiologists' annotations, performance is evaluated with both overlap- and distance-based metrics. Furthermore, the model is tested on synthetic mammograms and benchmarked against classical segmentation methods (Otsu thresholding, gradient vector flow active contour, and Chan-Vese segmentation), Fuzzy c-means clustering, and the state-of-the-art Medical Segment Anything (MedSAM) model. Results: By leveraging transfer learning, a limited dataset suffices for stable training, with the network converging by the 10th epoch. The optimal configuration achieves a bounding box average precision (BBox AP) of 0.80 and a segmentation average precision (Segm AP) of 0.58. Evaluated on a test set of real mammograms, the model correctly identifies the lesions, yielding an average Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 0.87 and an average intersection over union (IoU) of 0.77, performance aligned with the current state of the art. Conclusions: Mask R-CNN has emerged as a reliable and robust model for breast lesion segmentation; compared to the other methods evaluated in this study, it demonstrates superior performance across both overlap- and distance-based metrics. The model exhibits high DSC and IoU scores even on synthetic mammograms with a priori known lesion profiles, which can be used as an objective ground truth to mitigate annotation bias from inter-operator variability among radiologists.

title: From Counting Cells to Reconstructing Death: A Commentary on Artificial Intelligence in Forensic Histopathology.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is being investigated as a means to advance forensic histopathology from visual description to quantitative mapping, pattern recognition, and multimodal reconstruction of death. Recent developments in human postmortem analysis include validated whole-slide digitisation as foundational infrastructure and task-specific AI applications for diatom detection, glomerular quantification, coronary morphometry, myocardial classification, immunohistochemistry scoring, and virtual staining. AI-based postmortem interval (PMI) estimation remains experimental; the multi-organ study referenced in this commentary utilised an animal model, and human forensic validity has not yet been established. Foundation and vision-language models may ultimately extend these capabilities across organs and integrate microscopic findings with autopsy, toxicological, radiological, and circumstantial evidence. Postmortem tissue, however, is subject to autolysis, decomposition, agonal events, resuscitation, and non-standardised sampling, while the reference diagnosis is often a probabilistic whole-case opinion rather than an objective slide label. This work introduces FORENS-AI (FORensic Histopathology Evidence Network and Safeguards for AI), a conceptual architecture designed to convert computational outputs into traceable medicolegal evidence. FORENS-AI has not been empirically validated and is not presented as a standard, scoring system, clinical decision rule, or practice recommendation. The framework represents findings as an evidence graph, separates the Slide, Case, and Claim Gates, and proposes progressively stronger validation as outputs move from measurement to temporal, mechanistic, or causal inference. The primary aim is not to automate certification of death, but to identify safeguards to evaluate before AI-derived histological findings are permitted to inform expert opinion.

title: Quantitative MRI Characterization of Fluid-Related Phenotypes in Pediatric Epilepsy: Deep Learning-Assisted Assessment of Enlarged Perivascular Space Burden, Regional Distribution, and Clinical Associations.
abstract: Objective: To quantitatively characterize EPVS burden and regional distribution, together with CP and ventricular CSF structural imaging phenotypes, in pediatric epilepsy and to explore within-epilepsy clinical associations of EPVS measures differing from controls. Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 123 children with epilepsy and 108 controls aged 10-17 years. Enlarged perivascular space (EPVS), choroid plexus (CP), and ventricular cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) structural imaging phenotypes were quantitatively assessed using SHIVA-PVS, FreeSurfer, and 3D Slicer with expert visual quality control. Primary between-group comparisons used general linear models adjusted for age and sex, with estimated total intracranial volume additionally included for absolute volumetric measures, and multiple comparisons were controlled using the false discovery rate (FDR). Exploratory within-epilepsy clinical-association analyses were subsequently performed for EPVS measures showing FDR-significant between-group differences. Results: Global EPVS burden was higher in the epilepsy group than in controls ( q < 0.01), with the most pronounced regional differences in the basal ganglia (BG; q < 0.001). Relative distribution measures showed higher BG burden and lower centrum semiovale (CSO) burden and CSO/BG ratios in epilepsy ( q < 0.01). No statistically significant between-group differences were observed in the CP or ventricular CSF phenotypes. In exploratory within-epilepsy analyses, longer disease duration and drug resistance were associated predominantly with BG-EPVS measures, whereas associations with antiseizure medication burden were limited. Bilateral epileptiform activity was also associated with higher BG-EPVS burden after FDR correction ( q < 0.05). Conclusions: Primary between-group analyses identified greater EPVS burden in pediatric epilepsy, with the most pronounced regional differences involving the BG. Exploratory within-epilepsy analyses identified associations between selected EPVS measures and specific clinical characteristics. These cross-sectional structural imaging findings characterize a regional EPVS phenotype for further longitudinal and multimodal investigation but do not establish an underlying glymphatic mechanism.

title: Longitudinal Delta-Radiomics Identifies Treatment-Fraction-Associated Features Linked to Outcomes After Carbon-Ion Radiotherapy for Head and Neck Cancer.
abstract: Background : Longitudinal imaging during carbon-ion radiotherapy (CIRT) may capture dose-related tumor evolution before clinical assessment. We investigated whether serial CT-based Δ-radiomic features follow treatment-fraction (dose escalation)-associated trajectories with prognostic relevance in patients with head and neck cancer (HNC) treated with CIRT. Methods : We analyzed 167 HNC patients receiving 16-fraction CIRT. Features were extracted from plan-CT, confirm-CT, and weekly-CT scans after 5, 9, and 13 fractions. Δ-radiomic features were defined as time-normalized relative changes from confirm-CT. Linear mixed-effects models, paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, and monotonicity assessments identified features with systematic longitudinal changes. Endpoints were progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and local recurrence (LR). Optimal prediction timing was determined using optimism-corrected C-indices. Bootstrap resampling and multivariable Cox models assessed cutoff stability and incremental value beyond clinical factors. Results : During a median follow-up of 15.2 months (range: 1.2-67.7), 64 PFS events, 18 deaths, and 24 local recurrences occurred. Five, eight, and six candidate Δ-radiomic features were retained for PFS, OS, and LR. Selected prediction time points spanned fractions 5, 9, and 13. In multivariable analyses, four PFS-related features met the predefined robustness criteria and improved discrimination over the clinical model (C-index, 0.646-0.661 vs. 0.580; likelihood ratio test, p = 0.002-0.004). Sequential adjustment retained two OS-related and two LR-related features. Exploratory histology-specific analyses provided some support, primarily for two PFS-related features. Conclusions : Serial CT-based delta-radiomics identified treatment-fraction-associated imaging features associated with clinical endpoint risk after CIRT for HNC, particularly PFS. These findings are exploratory and require prospective external validation before clinical application.

title: Anomalous Origin of the Right Pulmonary Artery from the Ascending Aorta in an Adult After Prior Patent Ductus Arteriosus Surgery.
abstract: We present an adult patient with a history of surgical treatment of a patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) in whom contrast-enhanced chest computed tomography (CT) demonstrated anomalous origin of the right pulmonary artery (RPA) from the ascending aorta. Axial CT images clearly demonstrate an discontinuity between the main pulmonary artery and the right pulmonary artery (RPA), and delineate an abnormal opening on the ascending aorta; multiplanar reconstruction technology precisely locates the origin of the artery; dynamic volume imaging integrates the three-dimensional anatomical structure into a model nearly equivalent to a surgical perspective. This case illustrates that an anomalous pulmonary artery associated with a ductus may remain unrecognized at the time of ductus surgery and persist into adulthood, and that a single contrast-enhanced CT examination with multiplanar and cinematic reconstruction provides comprehensive, single-session confirmation of the diagnosis, together with the anatomic roadmap required for surgical planning. For any patient undergoing PDA closure-particularly when pulmonary hypertension or right-heart dilation seems disproportionate-deliberate verification of the origin of both pulmonary arteries may prevent a missed lesion and a second, avoidable operation.

title: Radiomics-Based Outcome Prediction in Transarterial Radioembolization (TARE) of Hepatic Malignancies: A Systematic Review and Quality Appraisal.
abstract: Background: Transarterial radioembolization (TARE) with Yttrium-90 ( 90 Y) microspheres is an established locoregional treatment for primary and secondary hepatic malignancies. Treatment response is heterogeneous, and accurate pre-procedural prediction of outcome remains a clinical challenge. Radiomics, defined as the high-throughput extraction of quantitative imaging features, may capture subvisual tumour heterogeneity that might be predictive of response, therefore enabling individualised patient selection and treatment planning. Objectives: To systematically review the current evidence on radiomics-based models derived from pre- and post-procedural imaging for predicting treatment response and survival outcomes in patients with primary and secondary hepatic lesions that were treated with TARE, and to evaluate the methodological quality of included studies. Methods: A systematic literature search was conducted across PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science. Studies reporting radiomics, texture analysis, dosiomics, or machine learning applied to imaging in patients with hepatic lesions treated with TARE, with at least one reported performance metric, were included. Methodological quality was assessed using the Radiomics Quality Score (RQS) and risk of bias and applicability using the Prediction model Risk Of Bias ASsessment Tool (PROBAST). Due to substantial heterogeneity, a narrative synthesis was performed. Results: Twenty-one studies encompassing 1734 patients were included (up to 73 patients may be counted twice because two cohorts overlap). Studies evaluated patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC; n = 12), intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCC; n = 2), colorectal cancer liver metastases (CLMs; n = 3), and mixed tumour cohorts ( n = 4). Imaging modalities included MRI ( n = 9), CT ( n = 5), 18 F-FDG PET or PET/CT ( n = 3), 90 Y PET or SPECT ( n = 2), cone-beam CT ( n = 1), and CT perfusion ( n = 1). All studies were retrospective, including two post hoc analyses of randomised trial cohorts, and none used external validation. Eighteen studies reported an area under the curve (AUC). The highest reported AUC ranged from 0.71 to 0.90 in eight studies with no validation, from 0.73 to 1.00 in six studies using internal cross-validation, and from 0.80 to 0.90 in four studies using an internal hold-out set. The median RQS was 2 (interquartile range 1 to 5; maximum 36), and all 21 studies had a high overall risk of bias on PROBAST. Conclusions: Radiomic models for predicting TARE outcomes show moderate to high apparent discrimination, but the evidence comes from small retrospective cohorts, is at high risk of bias, and has not been externally validated. Adding clinical variables to radiomic features produced only small gains. Prospective, multi-centre studies with standardised segmentation, harmonised radiomics pipelines, and robust external validation are needed before routine clinical adoption.

Studies evaluated patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC; n = 12), intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCC; n = 2), colorectal cancer liver metastases (CLMs; n = 3), and mixed tumour cohorts (n = 4). Imaging modalities included MRI (n = 9), CT (n = 5), 18F-FDG PET or PET/CT (n = 3), 90Y PET or SPECT (n = 2), cone-beam CT (n = 1), and CT perfusion (n = 1). All studies were retrospective, including two post hoc analyses of randomised trial cohorts, and none used external validation. Eighteen studies reported an area under the curve (AUC). The highest reported AUC ranged from 0.71 to 0.90 in eight studies with no validation, from 0.73 to 1.00 in six studies using internal cross-validation, and from 0.80 to 0.90 in four studies using an internal hold-out set. The median RQS was 2 (interquartile range 1 to 5; maximum 36), and all 21 studies had a high overall risk of bias on PROBAST. Conclusions: Radiomic models for predicting TARE outcomes show moderate to high apparent discrimination, but the evidence comes from small retrospective cohorts, is at high risk of bias, and has not been externally validated. Adding clinical variables to radiomic features produced only small gains. Prospective, multi-centre studies with standardised segmentation, harmonised radiomics pipelines, and robust external validation are needed before routine clinical adoption.

title: PACS-Integrated Artificial Intelligence-Based Software Tool for Rapid and Fully Automatic Bone Fracture Assessment of the Tibial Plateau.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Tibial plateau fractures (TPF) are complex intra-articular injuries requiring accurate reduction and stable fixation; inadequate planning can prolong recovery and increase osteoarthritis risk. Although CT-based 3D reconstructions are routine, automated 3D identification and separation of individual fracture fragments is uncommon. We evaluated a PACS-integrated AI workflow for automated 3D segmentation of intact bones, fracture detection, and fracture-fragment delineation. Methods: This single-center retrospective study analyzed preoperative TPF CT scans acquired on 64- and 128-slice scanners. Femur, patella, tibia, fibula, and fracture components were manually segmented in Visage 7 by a radiologist (9 years of experience) and an orthopedic surgeon (4 years). Segmentations were exported as NIfTI and used to train a 3D nnU-Net model with default preprocessing and parameters on 20 annotated TPF cases using a two-phase training strategy (initial training followed by retraining with refined labels). The trained model was integrated into Visage 7 and executed via an interactive PACS button for fully automated segmentation. Two independent readers rated outputs on a five-point Likert scale for intact bone segmentation, fracture detection, and fragment delineation; inter-reader association was assessed using Spearman and Kendall correlations. Results: In 108 fully rated cases, intact bone segmentation scored very high (means 4.67/4.72; median 5) and fracture detection was good (means 4.15/4.20; median 4). In contrast, individual fracture-fragment differentiation was limited (means 2.64/2.75; median 2). Inter-reader association was very high (Spearman r 0.943-0.967; Kendall's tau-b 0.875-0.971; all p < 0.001). Greater fracture complexity was associated with poorer fracture-fragment differentiation. Discussion: A PACS-integrated AI workflow can reliably segment intact bones and detect TPF within routine imaging, supporting rapid 3D visualization for surgical planning. However, robust separation of individual fracture fragments remains the primary limitation, motivating larger and more diverse training datasets and continued model refinement.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Enhanced Cardiac Magnetic Resonance in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: Diagnosis, Phenotypic Characterization, and Risk Prediction.
abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a genetically and phenotypically heterogeneous myocardial disease associated with a broad spectrum of clinical outcomes, including heart failure, atrial fibrillation, ventricular arrhythmias, and sudden cardiac death. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) plays a central role in the comprehensive assessment of HCM by enabling integrated evaluation of myocardial morphology, ventricular and atrial function, tissue characterization, myocardial deformation, and longitudinal disease progression within a single comprehensive imaging modality. However, conventional CMR interpretation remains limited by manual post-processing, interobserver variability, sequence-dependent measurements, and reliance on a relatively restricted set of predefined imaging parameters. These limitations may hinder the full exploitation of the rich multidimensional information contained in CMR datasets. Artificial intelligence (AI) approaches, particularly machine learning and deep learning, together with radiomics-based quantitative image analysis, provide new opportunities to extend the diagnostic and prognostic value of CMR to extract high-dimensional and quantitative information from cine imaging, late gadolinium enhancement, parametric mapping, and feature-tracking-based deformation analysis. Emerging evidence suggests that AI-enhanced CMR may facilitate automated image analysis, improve diagnostic classification, support differentiation of HCM from phenocopies, enable tissue- and deformation-based phenotypic characterization, and enhance individualized risk prediction. Although several studies have included independent or external testing, many remain retrospective, rely on selected populations or internal validation, and lack prospective assessment of clinical utility. High discrimination performance should not be interpreted as established clinical utility, because calibration, decision-curve analysis, clinically relevant thresholds, and prospective clinical impact remain insufficiently evaluated. In addition, interpretability and clinical generalizability remain important challenges for translation into routine practice. This review summarizes the current role of CMR in HCM and discusses emerging applications, methodological challenges, and future directions of AI-enhanced CMR for diagnosis, phenotypic characterization, and risk stratification.

title: AI-Driven Hyperspectral Imaging in Clinical Medicine: A Critical Appraisal of Translational Readiness.
abstract: The instruments used for intraoperative guidance have not improved over the years. Traditional margin evaluations fail in 10-20% of cancer surgeries, and histopathology confirmation can take 48-72 h. A promising alternative is hyperspectral imaging (HSI), which allows for real-time, label-free, non-contact, and detailed biochemical characterization of tissues. This review synthesizes 130 studies from 2015 to 2026, identified through a systematic search across multiple databases following PRISMA-ScR guidelines. The studies cover various clinical areas, including surgical oncology (53%), neurosurgery (10.8%), perfusion assessment (6.2%), gastroenterology (5.4%), dermatology (4.6%), and emerging domains (20%). Each clinical area is evaluated using a four-part Translational Readiness Appraisal framework. This framework shifts the focus from technical proficiency to deployment evidence by examining hardware compatibility with operating rooms, real-time workflow integration, cross-site validation, and regulatory readiness. Since 2015, the combination of clinically approved HSI hardware and artificial intelligence has led to a tenfold increase in publications. However, a significant gap remains: none of the reviewed studies meet the evidence criteria necessary for regulatory approval. Of the studies, 48.5% show strong single-site validation, but 50.8% remain in the proof-of-concept stage. The heavy reliance on intra-patient validation tends to inflate performance estimates, leaving issues like calibration across devices and regulatory pathways largely unaddressed. HSI has demonstrated technical maturity in several areas, particularly in head and neck margin assessment and brain tumor delineation. The primary reason for the lack of clinical adoption is not imaging performance but rather the absence of multicenter validation and a formal regulatory evidence framework.

title: Quantitative Glandular Tissue Component Assessment on Breast Ultrasound Using an Anatomically Constrained Deep Learning Framework.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Glandular tissue component (GTC) has been incorporated into BI-RADS v2025 as part of breast tissue composition assessment, but visual grading remains subjective and does not provide continuous quantification. We developed and evaluated an ROI-guided, anatomically constrained deep learning framework for quantitative GTC assessment on breast ultrasound. Reader performance was compared between unaided and AI-assisted sessions. Methods: This retrospective single-center study included 421 ultrasound images from 114 women for model development and 150 women for clinical evaluation. The framework segmented fibroglandular tissue (FGT) and glandular tissue to calculate continuous GTC percentage and assign the corresponding image-derived P1-P4 category. Four model configurations were compared during model development using patient-level five-fold cross-validation. Standalone AI performance was evaluated against expert consensus. Two senior and two junior radiologists assessed the clinical cohort without and with AI assistance, separated by a 4-week washout period. Results: During model development, the anatomical constraint markedly improved anatomical consistency while quantitative error and segmentation performance remained comparable. In the clinical cohort, continuous GTC percentage showed an MAE of 3.88 percentage points and strong correlation with the reference percentage (Spearman ρ = 0.957, p < 0.001). Exact P1-P4 agreement was 78.0%, adjacent agreement was 99.3%, and weighted κ was 0.888. However, 26 of 36 reference P4 cases (72.2%) were underestimated. Exact agreement was significantly higher for all four readers in the second, AI-assisted session than in the first, unaided session (all p < 0.001). Conclusions: The framework enabled anatomically consistent continuous GTC quantification and categorical assessment on individual breast ultrasound images.

title: Determinants and Prognostic Value of Persistent Congestion Assessed by Venous Excess Ultrasound Score in Acute Heart Failure.
abstract: Background: Reliable quantification of systemic venous congestion in acute heart failure (HF) has become feasible with the advent of the venous excess ultrasound (VExUS) score, informing therapeutic management. Nevertheless, the determinants of the VExUS score trajectory during hospitalization and the prognostic implications of persistent subclinical congestion at discharge remain poorly defined. Methods: Consecutive patients admitted for acute HF were prospectively enrolled ( n = 418, 73.3 ± 11.8 years old, 59.1% male). VExUS scores were assessed at admission and prior to discharge to categorize the patients into three groups: non-congested (persistent score of 0; n = 81), improved (score reduction of ≥1 point; n = 214), and non-improved (persistent congestion without score reduction; n = 123). Baseline clinical data were collected and all the patients had a transthoracic echocardiogram on admission. All patients were followed up post-discharge and the primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality or HF hospitalization. Results: Patients with non-improved VExUS exhibited a higher burden of right-sided remodeling and dysfunction including larger right chambers, lower right ventricle (RV) systolic function indices, higher RV systolic pressures and a higher prevalence of severe tricuspid regurgitation (all p < 0.001). Severe tricuspid regurgitation was the sole independent predictor of VExUS non-improvement (OR 2.86, 95% CI 1.51-5.45, p = 0.001). Non-improved VExUS (HR 1.77; 95% CI 1.17-2.67; p = 0.007), severe tricuspid regurgitation (HR 1.88; 95% CI 1.16-3.02; p = 0.010) and intravenous furosemide dose (HR 1.00; 95% CI 1.00-1.01; p = 0.011) were independent predictors of the composite primary endpoint. Inclusion of non-improved VExUS provided incremental prognostic value over models including clinical, laboratory, and echocardiographic parameters (Δχ 2 = 9.22; p = 0.007). Conclusions: VExUS non-improvement throughout hospitalization marks patients with worse primary endpoint Severe tricuspid regurgitation emerges as an independent determinant of VExUS non-improvement which is independently associated with poor long-term outcomes.

title: Extravascular Cyanoacrylate "Embolization" for the Treatment of Vesico-Vaginal Fistula: A Minimally Invasive Alternative.
abstract: Vesico-vaginal fistula (VVF) is a debilitating complication commonly occurring after gynecologic surgery and frequently associated with significant morbidity and impaired quality of life. Although surgical repair remains the standard treatment, management strategies remain heterogeneous, while conservative approaches often require prolonged urinary diversion with variable success rates. We report a case of persistent post-surgical VVF successfully treated with image-guided embolization using N-butyl cyanoacrylate methylsulfone (NBCA; Glubran 2, GEM; Viareggio, Italy) through a transvesical catheter-based approach after failure of conservative management. This case illustrates the potential role of interventional radiology in the management of selected VVFs, suggesting that image-guided fistula embolization may represent a minimally invasive treatment option when conservative management fails and surgical reintervention is undesirable or can be deferred.

title: AdaSwitch3D: Reliability-Aware Human-in-the-Loop Artificial Intelligence for Breast Tumor Segmentation in Dynamic Contrast-Enhanced MRI Across Unseen Centers.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Deep learning models for breast tumor segmentation in dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) often lose accuracy at centers that did not contribute training data. We investigated whether case-wise routing between two low-resource adapted models, combined with an uncertainty-based review-prioritization signal, behaves consistently under severe cross-center domain shift. Methods: Using the four public collections of the MAMA-MIA dataset (DUKE, ISPY1, ISPY2, NACT; 1231 cases), we performed four-fold leave-one-center-out experiments in which each held-out center contributed only five labeled cases and a pool of unlabeled scans. We compared source-only transfer, five-shot fine-tuning, and teacher-student self-training with AdaSwitch3D, which routes each case between the two adapted branches using 17 label-free features and produces a heuristic review-prioritization signal. The complete pipeline-data splits, five-shot selection, training, adaptation, router construction, and referral calibration-was repeated with five random seeds, and each seed was evaluated once on 80 untouched test cases (400 seed-specific test observations). Results: Across five independent repetitions, mean Dice was 0.325 ± 0.051 for source-only transfer, 0.353 ± 0.052 for five-shot fine-tuning, 0.372 ± 0.047 for teacher-student adaptation, and 0.377 ± 0.057 for AdaSwitch3D; a validation-selected per-center strategy reached 0.376 ± 0.044. AdaSwitch3D exceeded five-shot fine-tuning in all five seeds and teacher-student adaptation in four, but the difference between AdaSwitch3D and teacher-student adaptation was small (mean +0.005) and varied by seed, while inference required both branches (approximately twice the single-model time). Observed test referral rates ranged from 23.8% to 56.3% against a 20% validation target, and low-Dice (<0.20) failure capture ranged from 21.7% to 71.8%. In the prespecified case-level analysis of seed 42, AdaSwitch3D improved on source-only transfer and five-shot fine-tuning (Holm-adjusted p=0.021 for each), whereas the comparison with teacher-student adaptation did not provide evidence of a difference (Holm-adjusted p=0.508). Conclusions: Absolute segmentation accuracy remained low, the incremental benefit of case-wise routing over teacher-student adaptation was small and seed-dependent, and referral behavior was unstable across repetitions. The principal finding is therefore that cross-center adaptation, case-wise model selection, and heuristic referral remain sensitive under limited target supervision. AdaSwitch3D should be interpreted as an exploratory case study of these challenges rather than as a clinically validated segmentation or referral system.

title: Generative Forecasting of Longitudinal 3D-OCT Under Anti-VEGF Therapy for Diabetic Macular Edema.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Forecasting the individual anatomical response to anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy from optical coherence tomography (OCT) could support the management of diabetic retinal disease. Direct volumetric generation is difficult because treatment-associated change is local while most of the retina is stationary, so generative models regress to the mean and blur retinal layers. Methods: We propose a two-stage framework that decouples baseline anatomy from longitudinal change in 3D-OCT. A Retinal Response Tokenizer compresses the latent residual between baseline and follow-up volumes into discrete action tokens via Finite Scalar Quantization (FSQ), and a conditional decoder renders the follow-up volume from baseline features and these tokens. An Action Transformer predicts the tokens from the baseline scan, the follow-up interval, and baseline covariates. Results: On the OLIVES trial cohort (diabetic retinopathy and macular edema; 738 test pairs from five held-out eyes), our method achieved the highest structural similarity in every test eye (SSIM 0.657 vs. 0.543-0.623) and tracked the central subfield thickness (CST) change measured by a frozen regressor (Δ-r=0.88). In a five-fold cross-validation over 52 eyes, it improved PSNR over an identity copy by 1.27 dB (95% CI 0.93-1.57) and reduced the CST change error by 10.5 μm (95% CI 3.1-19.4). Conclusions: Prospective validation is required before clinical use.

title: Detector-Stage Failures Account for Most of the Increase in the External Deficit of a Box-Prompted Glioma Segmentation Pipeline on BraTS-Africa: A Three-Arm Decomposition Across Two External Cohorts.
abstract: Background/Objectives: When a box-prompted segmentation pipeline loses accuracy on new data, the detector proposing the box or a later stage may be responsible; this study measured which. Methods: A real-time detection transformer (RT-DETR) feeding the Segment Anything Model 2.1 was compared with a detector-free model (MedSAM3 with a low-rank adapter) on whole-tumor Dice in 158 patients with glioma: held-out Brain Tumor Segmentation (BraTS) 2020 cases ( n = 24), the RHUH-GBM glioblastoma cohort ( n = 39), and BraTS-Africa ( n = 95, glioma presumed). Giving the segmenter the ground-truth box splits the Dice gap between the systems into a detector-stage term and a residual. Results: The detector-stage term was +0.006 Dice on held-out cases, +0.018 on RHUH-GBM, and +0.091 on BraTS-Africa. Its increase over the held-out value was +0.0854 [95% CI +0.0450, +0.1303] on BraTS-Africa (Holm-adjusted p < 0.001) and, after correction of a preprocessing fault, +0.0120 [-0.0062, +0.0295] on RHUH-GBM, which was not resolved. On BraTS-Africa, it came mainly from slices without a detector box. No residual change was resolved. Conclusions: On BraTS-Africa, the detector stage accounted for most of the increase in the pipeline's gap; on RHUH-GBM, no increase was resolved. The decomposition should be measured per cohort.

title: AI-Based Automated Segmentation of the Mandibular Cortex and Mental Foramen for Radiomorphometric Measurement on Panoramic Radiographs: A Feasibility Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives : This study evaluated the feasibility of a YOLOv5-based model for automated segmentation of these structures and automated measurement of mandibular cortical width (MCW) and panoramic mandibular index PMI. Methods : Five hundred panoramic radiographs were retrospectively collected. The mandibular cortex and the right and left mental foramina were annotated with polygon labels as three separate classes and verified by an experienced radiologist; intra- and inter-observer reliability was evaluated on a random 10% subset. A YOLOv5s-seg model was trained for 500 epochs and evaluated on an independent, patient-level test set. Model performance was quantified with precision, recall, F1 score, Dice coefficient, mean intersection over union (mIoU), and mean average precision (mAP@0.5 and mAP@0.5:0.95). Results : The model achieved a precision of 0.94, a recall of 0.82, and an F1 score of 0.88 (mAP@0.5 = 0.86; mAP@0.5:0.95 = 0.52). The Dice coefficient was 0.93 for the mandibular cortex and 0.80 and 0.75 for the right and left mental foramina, respectively. In the side-level paired agreement analysis (62 measurable sides from 44 test-set patients), the ICC was 0.89 (95% CI: 0.84-0.93) for MCW, with a mean bias of +0.08 mm and 0.87 for PMI, with a mean bias of +0.01. Conclusions : YOLOv5 showed high agreement with expert observers for mandibular cortex segmentation and moderate agreement for the mental foramen, supporting the technical feasibility of automated MCW and PMI measurement. Because missed mental foramen detections reduce the number of measurable sites, automated measurement should be combined with a verification step.

title: Fusion of Deep Learning Radiomics and Clinical Features for Individualized Prediction of Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy Response in Osteosarcoma.
abstract: Background: Stage IIB conventional osteosarcoma exhibits highly heterogeneous responses to neoadjuvant chemotherapy, necessitating reliable, noninvasive pre-treatment evaluation systems. Methods: This retrospective study of 198 patients utilized pre-treatment T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and baseline clinical data. Twelve classical convolutional neural network architectures were benchmarked to identify the optimal imaging backbone. This selected radiomics score was then integrated with core clinical variables using logistic regression to construct a multimodal model. Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping++ (Grad-CAM++) and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) algorithms provided image- and feature-level interpretability. Results: DenseNet121 achieved the highest mean cross-validated area under the curve (AUC; 0.775) and was selected, with AUCs of 0.797 (95% CI: 0.716-0.877) and 0.701 (95% CI: 0.513-0.877) in the training and test cohorts. Adding the clinical variables improved discrimination, yielding a test-cohort AUC of 0.827 (95% CI: 0.661-0.992) with significant reclassification gain over the radiomics-only model (NRI = 1.28, IDI = 0.177; DeLong p = 0.011). Grad-CAM++ activation concentrated on the solid medullary and extraosseous soft-tissue components, and SHAP ranked the radiomics score as the strongest contributor. Conclusions: Integrating deep learning radiomics with key clinical features provides a noninvasive tool for the individualized prediction of neoadjuvant chemosensitivity in osteosarcoma.

title: CT Ventricular Volume Reference Percentile Curves Using Automated nnU-Net Segmentation: A Study with LLM-Facilitated Cohort Selection.
abstract: Background: Age- and sex-specific CT reference percentile curves of ventricular volume may support objective assessment of ventricular enlargement. We aimed to generate such curves by combining a locally deployed large language model (LLM) for cohort curation with nnU-Net 12-subcompartment segmentation. Methods: This retrospective study did not require formal ethics approval under the Swiss Human Research Act. We screened 42,211 head CT reports from January 2019 to April 2024. A phrase prefilter identified 9622 candidates for German-tuned 70-billion-parameter LLM review of stroke, leukoencephalopathy, parenchymal defects, enlarged ventricles, and space-occupying lesions; 6516 remained. A second LLM workflow screened 210,761 clinical data warehouse summaries to exclude dementia, organic brain disease, or cognitive decline. After image-availability and series-mismatch exclusions, the final cohort comprised 2608 CTs from 2608 patients (1374 males, 1234 females; age 14-98 years). Ventricular masks were obtained using a validated nnU-Net tool integrated in TotalSegmentator. Results: LLM labelling accuracy in 471 blinded reports ranged from 0.966 to 0.992. CDW screening audit showed 91% agreement, sensitivity 0.96, and negative predictive value 0.96. Median total ventricular volume rose from 10.94 mL in young females and 13.42 mL in young males to 21.97 mL and 31.97 mL, respectively, in the 60-69 age group. Except for the fourth ventricle, compartments showed positive age correlations ( r = 0.44-0.69); the fourth ventricle showed no relevant association ( r = 0.01 males; r = 0.05 females). After adjustment for age, male sex remained associated with greater total ventricular volume (6.54 mL; 95% CI, 5.61-7.46; p<0.001). Conclusions: This study provides age- and sex-specific CT ventricular nomograms in a selected reference cohort. The LLM-assisted curation and nnU-Net segmentation workflow provides a feasible approach for large-scale cohort analysis.

title: AI-Assisted Triage for Diabetic Retinopathy Integrated into Routine Diabetes Care: A Real-World Diagnostic Accuracy Study of the DAIRET ® Algorithm.
abstract: Background : Screening for diabetic retinopathy (DR) is resource-intensive. We evaluated the real-world diagnostic accuracy of the DAIRET ® Artificial Intelligence (AI) algorithm, integrated into the electronic medical record, as a triage tool in routine diabetes care. Methods : Retrospective, STARD-AI-compliant study of consecutive adults with diabetes screened with non-mydriatic fundus photography between April and December 2025. The DAIRET ® output ("suspected"/"not suspected") was compared with grading by an ophthalmologist masked to the AI result. Sensitivity, specificity and predictive values with exact 95% confidence intervals were calculated for any DR and referable (moderate or worse) DR. Results : Among 1051 patients, 185 (17.6%) had DR: 160 mild and 25 moderate non-proliferative DR; none had severe DR. DAIRET ® classified 271 patients (25.8%) as suspected. For any DR, sensitivity was 59.5% (52.0-66.6) and specificity 81.4% (78.7-83.9). For referable DR, sensitivity was 100.0% (86.3-100.0), specificity 76.0% (73.3-78.6) and negative predictive value 100.0% (99.5-100.0). Specificity was lower in patients aged <65 years and with type 1 diabetes. Conclusions : No referable case was missed, although sensitivity was based on 25 cases (lower limit 86.3%) and 15 AI-negative patients lacked complete verification. The 74% classified as "not suspected" is a potential, not measured, reduction in referrals. Performance for severe or proliferative DR could not be assessed, and multi-center confirmation is needed.

Conclusions: No referable case was missed, although sensitivity was based on 25 cases (lower limit 86.3%) and 15 AI-negative patients lacked complete verification. The 74% classified as "not suspected" is a potential, not measured, reduction in referrals. Performance for severe or proliferative DR could not be assessed, and multi-center confirmation is needed.

title: Label-Scarce Ultrasound Biopsy Needle Identification Using Dynamics-Guided Prior Modeling.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Ultrasound-guided biopsy is essential for accurate needle placement in minimally invasive procedures. However, the limited availability of labeled medical data significantly constrains the development of needle segmentation models, and existing semi-supervised approaches rely solely on data-driven consistency constraints without incorporating domain-specific dynamic properties of the imaging process. We propose a semi-supervised unrolling optimization framework that combines dynamics-based data consistency with self-training. Methods: (1) A null-space projection-based Analytic Model (A) layer is unrolled into the network to suppress background interference and enforce dynamics-based constraints derived from temporal ultrasound sequences, in which the background subspace is estimated via singular value decomposition (SVD) of consecutive frames and the needle signal is recovered by projecting the observed image onto the orthogonal complement of this subspace. (2) A self-training strategy leverages unlabeled ultrasound data by generating soft pseudo-labels from a pretrained teacher network to iteratively supervise the student model, which shares the same unrolling architecture and is jointly trained with a supervised loss on labeled data and a pseudo loss on unlabeled data. Results: Evaluation on an ultrasound needle segmentation dataset demonstrated that the proposed method achieved a Dice score of 0.7429±0.0489 and an IoU of 0.5967±0.0917, outperforming the supervised UnrollNet baseline (Dice: 0.7298±0.0518), Co-Training (U-Net) (Dice: 0.6104±0.0949), and Meta Pseudo Labels (Dice: 0.6426±0.1140). The proposed method also yielded a mean trajectory angle error of 0.66∘±0.63∘ and a tip position error of 0.95mm±0.74mm. Conclusions: These results indicate the potential of the proposed framework for ultrasound-guided needle tracking.

title: The Role of Reprojected Planar Data Derived from Fast Whole-Body Bone SPECT/CT.
abstract: Background/Objectives: The purpose of this prospective study was to investigate the preferred reconstruction SPECT parameters for generating reprojected planar images in bone studies, and to evaluate, by visual reader assessment, the feasibility of using these reprojected images as a substitute for traditional planar whole-body (WB) bone scan images. This was a single-centre feasibility study; diagnostic accuracy was not assessed. Methods: Patients referred for planar bone scintigraphy (PBS) and WB-SPECT/CT were prospectively enrolled. Reprojected planar bone scintigraphy (R-PBS) data were generated using forward projection of the three-bed SPECT/CT data. Three nuclear medicine (NM) specialists, blinded to the imaging reconstruction, evaluated both sets of images in a randomised order. The preferred reconstruction parameters for R-PBS were determined by visual assessment using a 4-point ordinal visual scoring scale. A side-by-side comparison of PBS vs. R-PBS was conducted, including assessments of image quality, artefact generation, image preference, and any clinical significance that may affect report interpretation. The agreement between the physicians' evaluations was measured using the Kappa coefficient test. Results : Of the four reconstruction parameter combinations, 6 iterations, 8 subsets, and a 5 mm Gaussian post-filter yielded the highest visual quality scores. PBS images scored higher on image quality, though this difference was not statistically significant ( p > 0.05). The inter-rater agreement for image quality scores was moderate for both PBS and R-PBS images. The results indicate that among the 33 reader-level assessments derived from 11 patient pairs and reviewed by the 3 readers, PBS images were preferred 13 times (~40%), R-PBS 10 times (30%), and no preference was indicated for the remaining 10 (30%). Conclusions : In this small feasibility cohort, R-PBS images derived from fast WB-SPECT/CT data were of visual quality comparable to PBS and may have potential as an alternative to PBS. If confirmed in larger studies with formal diagnostic accuracy assessment, R-PBS could remove the need for a separate PBS acquisition and reduce overall patient imaging time.

title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery-A Narrative Review.
abstract: Background : The use of artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly growing in the field of dental medicine and in oral and maxillofacial surgery (OMS). The aim of the present review is to assess current applications of AI in OMS, to evaluate their advantages and limitations, and to identify areas requiring further research. Materials and Methods : A comprehensive search was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar, with targeted keywords including "artificial intelligence," "deep learning," "machine learning," "oral surgery," "maxillofacial surgery," and "diagnosis "Artificial Intelligence" OR "Machine Learning" OR "Deep Learning" AND "Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery" OR "Oral Surgery" OR "Maxillofacial Surgery" AND "Diagnosis". Of 308 identified studies, 37 met the inclusion criteria focusing on AI-assisted detection interpretation and surgical planning in OMS. Results : AI is effective in identifying anatomical landmarks, evaluating lesions and cysts, diagnosing bone disease like medication-related osteonecrosis of jaws (MRONJ), planning dental implants, and aiding in the classification of fractures and temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disorders. AI can match or outperform human experts in various diagnostic tasks, particularly in panoramic and cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) image analysis. AI shows promise in early detection of impacted and supernumerary teeth, maxillofacial pathologies, neoplastic conditions, and soft tissue calcifications. Limitations: However, substantial methodological heterogeneity, inconsistent reporting of AI performance metrics, and limited external validation across the included studies constrain direct comparison of results and assessment of the generalizability of reported AI performance. Conclusions: AI may assist clinicians in diagnostic and treatment-related decision-making, but current evidence does not support its use as a replacement for comprehensive clinical assessment and professional judgment.

title: AI-Augmented Digital Diagnostics in Minimally Invasive Dentistry: A Case Report on Clinically Occult Approximal Caries.
abstract: Background Approximal dental caries pose a persistent diagnostic challenge, as early lesions frequently remain clinically occult beneath intact enamel surfaces during routine visual-tactile inspection. This case report describes the clinical utility, limitations, and decision-making discrepancies within a multimodal digital diagnostic workflow combining intraoral radiography, near-infrared light transillumination (NILT), and deep-learning artificial intelligence (AI) radiographic analysis. Case presentation A 19-year-old female patient presented with provoked cold and sweet sensitivity localized to the upper left quadrant. Clinical inspection revealed visually intact accessible enamel surfaces (ICDAS 0 on tooth 25. To resolve the discrepancy between subjective symptoms and inconclusive initial visual findings, periapical radiography and NILT were performed. After the clinician-led treatment plan had been established, the radiograph was additionally processed using ClinicalAID as a parallel research analysis. Diagnostic Assessment and Management: Periapical radiography and NILT revealed approximal demineralization on teeth 24, 25, and 26. After the clinician-led treatment plan had been established, the radiograph was additionally processed with ClinicalAID as a parallel research analysis, yielding model confidence scores of 100%, 99%, and 98% for teeth 24, 25, and 26, respectively. Pre-operative therapeutic stratification remained entirely clinician-led: teeth 24 and 25 were selected for operative intervention based on provoked symptomatology and radiographic appearance of dentinal involvement, whereas tooth 26 was managed non-operatively with topical fluoridation and scheduled monitoring. Operative clinical reference assessment confirmed demineralization extending into the middle third of the dentin on tooth 25. Conclusions High AI caries-detection confidence scores do not differentiate between lesion depth, cavitation status, or the necessity of operative intervention, as evidenced by divergent clinical pathways despite near-identical AI output scores on teeth 25 and 26. Deep-learning algorithms must function strictly as adjunctive decision-support tools within a human-in-the-loop framework (Intelligence Augmentation), with treatment planning governed by clinical symptoms, caries risk, and conventional diagnostic synthesis.

title: Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence Tools in Imaging Reporting: Practical Guidelines for Sonographers-A Narrative Review.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly entering diagnostic ultrasound, supporting image acquisition, automated measurement, computer-aided diagnosis, and report drafting. Sonographers are primary users of these tools, yet sonographer-oriented guidance on their responsible use in imaging reporting remains fragmented. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence, reporting guidelines, trustworthiness frameworks, regulations, and professional standards relevant to AI-assisted imaging reporting to distill practical guidance for sonographers. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched, together with professional-body and regulatory documents published up to July 2026. The review maps AI applications across the reporting chain, from real-time acquisition guidance (AI-guided echocardiography achieving diagnostic-quality images in 98.8% of novice-obtained scans) to computer-aided diagnosis improving breast lesion assessment (area under the curve increasing from 0.83 to 0.87) and large language models drafting structured reports. Evidence on automation bias, deskilling, hallucinated content, algorithmic bias, and medico-legal accountability is critically appraised. Building on FUTURE-AI, CONSORT-AI, DECIDE-AI, and World Health Organization guidance, a phase-based good-practice framework is proposed, covering pre-use appraisal and training, verification during use, and documentation and audit after use. AI should augment, not replace, sonographer judgment; human oversight, verification of every AI output, transparent documentation, and continuing AI literacy are prerequisites for safe adoption in imaging reporting.
